The low power application considered in this paper is the case of off-grid rural electrification, where a person in a rural area uses a bicycle-based human power generating system to charge a battery for the purpose of lighting his home with a few low-wattage LED lamps during periods of necessity. In this regard, two methods to convert energy from human muscle activity into useful electricity by utilizing the commonly available bicycle are proposed and presented with hardware results. The presented hardware results prove that power of the order of 50 W can be successfully generated using these methods. Another important feature is that, the methodology involved in generating useful electricity is carbon-free and power can be generated at any given point of time regardless of location or the associated climatic condition.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Slip-Ring Induction Motors with Stator and Rotor Inter-turn Faults for Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, an SRIM model with major electrical faults based on reference frame theory is presented. To model shorted turns, the model assumes that each stator/rotor phase winding has a different number of turns. The impact of the electrical fault on the signals of the motor including speed, electromagnetic torque, and stator currents are addressed. The obtained simulation results from the proposed analytical model are compared and validated with finite element simulations with satisfactory results. The proposed models can be successfully used to study the transient, steady state behavior of the slip-ring induction motors with critical electrical faults, and to test fault diagnostic algorithms operating in real-time.

articleTitle: Model-Based Bearing Fault Detection in Induction Motors Under Speed Varying Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A novel model-based strategy for bearing fault detection in induction motor is presented. The proposed technique is based on state estimation of induction motor using non-linear derivative free kalman filter. Non-invasive fault detection is the critical advantage of the proposed strategy. The method is robust towards unbalanced supply and variable speed. Analytical computations are carried on 4 hp squirrel-cage induction motor using MATLAB software for different bearing faults. The presented simulation results are validated using auto correlation coefficients. Additionally, the proposed strategy provides better estimates for all types of bearing faults.

articleTitle: Model-Based Fault Detection and Diagnosis of Slip-Ring Induction Motors: A Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new non-invasive model-based fault detection and diagnosis of stator and rotor inter-turn faults in slip ring induction motors (SRIMs) are presented. Analytical modeling of SRIM with electrical faults is formulated. Innovation sequence generated from extended Kalman filter is used for accurate fault detection. Further, fault diagnosis is carried out using Brute-force search algorithm. Simulation results show that the presented method is an effective diagnosis procedure for major electrical faults in SRIMs. Robustness towards supply imbalance and speed varying conditions are the significant advantages of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Detection in Induction Motors Using Discrete-time Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel model-based strategy for bearing fault detection in induction motor is presented. The proposed method is based on state estimation of induction motor using discrete-time extended kalman filter. Non-invasive fault detection is the critical advantage of the proposed strategy. The method is robust towards unbalanced supply and variable speed. Analytical computations are carried on 4 hp squirrel-cage induction motor using MATLAB software for different bearing faults. The presented simulation results are validated using auto correlation coefficients. Additionally, the proposed strategy provides better estimates for all types of bearing faults.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Modelling and Control of a High Voltage Gain Dual Input Boost DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the small-signal model of single voltage multiplier high voltage gain dual input boost DC-DC converter. The model is developed with parasitic parameters by the state space averaging technique followed by small-signal linearization. For this nonlinear and non-minimum phase converter an inner current loop and outer voltage loop control strategy with PI and compensators are designed in MATLAB. Simulation results corresponding to a step load change between 50 % and full load are presented which ensure proper voltage regulation by controlling the duty cycle of switching the two sources.

articleTitle: Simplified Controller Design Approach for Quadratic Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In distributed generation, a quadratic boost converter (QBC) finds wide application due to its unique characteristic of higher boost voltage with lower duty cycle. For dc- dc converter, output voltage regulation with current limiting capability is an important requirement. The peak current control (PCC) offers good current limiting capability with faster output voltage control. In this paper, the PCC of the QBC is explored which has two control loop: inner current loop and outer voltage loop. The aim of the study was to provide a simplified step-by-step outer loop controller design procedure for QBC. In this approach, the optimum value of outer loop controller gain was derived by utilizing the QBC model. The effectiveness of the derived controller parameter was tested in MATLAB/Simulink environment by providing a step change in: input voltage, magnitude of load current and reference output voltage.

articleTitle: Detection of Power Quality Disturbances in Utility Grid with Wind Energy Penetration
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a method for detection of power quality (PQ) disturbances in power system network interfaced with wind energy power plant. Proposed algorithm uses multiresolution capability of discrete wavelet transform (DWT). PQ disturbances associated with operational events of wind energy generator such as outage and grid synchronization are analyzed. PQ issue associated with islanding event in the presence of wind energy has also been identified. The study is done with the help of an IEEE-13 node test system interfaced with wind generator in MATLAB / Simulink environment. Phase-A voltage signal caught on point of common coupling (PCC) was decomposed using DWT to receive detail coefficients up to fourth level of decomposition and approximation coefficient at fourth level of decomposition. The approximation coefficient at fourth level and detail coefficients at first and fourth level of decomposition are used to analyze the power quality issues associated with hybrid power system. The frequency and root mean square values of the voltage signal of phase-A are also analyzed for the recognition of the PQ problems.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of High gain DC-DC Converter in Mixed Signal Domain Control for PV based Microgrid Application
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A high gain, modular and compact isolated DC-DC (Direct Current) converter with wireless power control scheme is proposed here. DC-DC converters have an important role in DC microgrid systems. Inputs from renewable energy sources like solar photo voltaic (PV) system and fuel cell is in the form of DC in the order of a few tens of volts. This low voltage cannot be used directly for microgrid applications. Hence, it needs to be boosted to the required high voltage (few hundreds of volts) by using DC-DC boost converters. However, the boosted voltage is limited to two to three times of input voltage due to the stability limitation of non-isolated converters. Hence, isolated high gain DC-DC converter control in mixed signal domain is proposed in this article. Further, the output voltage of the converter and current can be controlled wirelessly through digital signal processor (DSP) based on android/computer application. A detailed design of the converter, both in state space analysis and in hardware, is put forward. Further, the proposed converter is experimentally tested for various input conditions and its results are explained in detail.

articleTitle: A SyRM Drive Based Solar PV Array Fed Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a position sensorless synchronous reluctance motor (SyRM) based solar photovoltaic (PV) array fed irrigation pumping system. Here, a single voltage source inverter (VSI) is utilized, which is responsible for the vector control of SyRM as well as extraction of peak power from the PV generator. The angular position and speed of the rotor, are estimated in real time from the motor currents and DC bus voltage signals. This reduces the number of sensors to four (twomotor currents, DC bus voltage and PV current). The incremental conductance algorithm is aided by a speed feedforward term to improve the dynamic performance of the proposed system under varying environmental conditions. Moreover, the control is inherently unaffected to the ageing related variation in pump constant. The suitability of the proposed water pumping system is tested through the experimental results, recorded on a developed prototype in the laboratory, under varying solar insolation.

Author Keywords: Vector control algorithm and Water pumping

articleTitle: Improving Performance of UPQC-DG for Compensation of Unbalanced Loads
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, an improved Power Angle Control (PAC) method for UPQC-DG has been proposed for effective compensation of unbalanced loads. UPQC-DG provides a simultaneous solution to power quality and renewable integration. PAC methods have been developed for UPQC-DG to enhance VA utilization of series and shunt APFs of UPQC-DG. In case of unbalanced loads, existing PAC methods result in circulation of reactive power and increased VA loading of UPQC-DG. PAC method proposed in this work, is designed to tackle above-mentioned issues. Also, proposed PAC method is based on Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) theory, which makes it robust to non-ideal voltages. Performance of proposed PAC method has been tested using real time simulation performed in Opal-RT. Simulation results show superior performance of UPQC-DG in presence of unbalanced and non-linear loads using proposed PAC method.

articleTitle: Space Vector based Zero Sequence Voltage Elimination Technique for an Even Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work proposes a Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation based scheme to eliminate the inherent problem of zero sequence voltage in an even level inverter. The scheme is presented for a 4-level inverter. Here, zero sequence voltage eliminated 4-level inversion is attained by switching amongst space vector combinations of a 7-level inverter having no zero-sequence voltage. The resulting space phasor diagram is generated, by realizing an intermediate space phasor diagram followed by translation of its vectors to switching states having no zero-sequence voltage, by simple mathematical algorithm. The scheme employs an open-end winding induction motor fed by cascaded three-level inverters from either side thereby, realizing a 7-level inverter configuration. All computations in this scheme are carried out in 60° co-ordinate system.

articleTitle: Reference Signal Generation for BLDC Motor Drives based on Different Sector Identification Methodologies using Hall Based Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are among the most widely accepted motor in automotive industries for propulsion of electric vehicles. BLDC motor requires knowledge of sector (rotor position) to perform current commutation using power electronics converter which can be determined in different ways. Hall sensors are usually used for sector identification. Earlier works exists on determining the sector using hall sensors but, different mathematical computation for sector identification based on hall sensors feedback were not reported. This paper presents and compares few existing techniques of sector identification using hall sensor. Further, binary to decimal converter based sector identification method for BLDC motor drives is proposed having minimum mathematical computational effort. Finally, the simulation results using MATLAB/Simulink environment are incorporated and experimental results using 24V, 4000 rpm BLDC motor, DRV8301 based BLDC drives and control algorithm implementation on F28335 platform are presented to validate the effectiveness of different sector identification techniques.

articleTitle: 100 kW Induction Motor for Hybrid Electric Tracked Vehicle - Design Steps and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In recent times, hybridization of conventional fuel vehicles are becoming more popular in automotive industries. A significant aspect of the development of Hybrid vehicles is the design of Electric motors and the control mechanism. This paper discusses the challenges in the design and performance estimation of a 100 kW induction motor for the purpose of traction. The paper assumes general performance requirements of a traction application and discusses the electromagnetic and mechanical considerations in the design process of an induction motor.

articleTitle: Multi-functional Bi-directional DC-DC/AC Converter Topology for Single Phase Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: DERs installation at the consumer premises involves two major converter sections, i.e., inverter and choppers, which need to be controlled accurately for efficient operation. This paper proposes a new non-isolated multifunctional input - output bi-directional DC-DC/AC converter topology for single phase islanded and grid-connected microgrid applications. A single converter module is capable of operating in all inversion, rectification, battery charging and discharging modes. This would ultimately reduce the number of controlled switches required for efficient power management and control of single phase hybrid DC / AC residential consumer premises. Control strategy for converter power coordination and control involves a series of logical decisions, made by sensing the power requirements of various generation / load units connected to the proposed converter topology. The proposed converter topology along with designed residential microgrid system has been verified through the simulations done on MATLAB platform.

articleTitle: Output Power Maximization of Wind Energy Conversion System Using Doubly Fed Induction Generator
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: COEP - Microgrid is a project by the students of College of Engineering, Pune. It aims at establishing a Microgrid in college campus, investigating different topologies for energy generation from renewable energy sources. Project Microgrid has a Wind Energy subsystem connected on the AC bus, to generate power from wind energy. Out of various topologies available for generation of wind power, Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) system is proposed, owing to its various advantages over other topologies. DFIG has the capability of extracting maximum power from the wind turbine, with reduced power converter rating requirements and their advantages in terms of efficiency and overall costs. This paper presents modelling, simulation and implementation of DFIG system for wind power generation. It also discusses about a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm for maximizing power output from the wind turbine based on wind speed. Finally implementation of system is done in laboratory in super-synchronous mode of operation.

articleTitle: 18-Sector Direct Torque Controlled Strategy with Improved Stator Flux Estimator for Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In direct torque control (DTC) scheme, stator flux vector, and electromagnetic torque are regulated by choosing a voltage vector from a switching logic table. However, the selected voltage vector is not always the perfect one because of only the sector is considered where the flux space vector lies without considering its precise position. Voltage vector selection depends on how precisely the flux is estimated. This paper describes a modified flux estimator scheme for DTC-based induction-motor drives. The flux estimated by the improved flux estimator is used to choose the stator voltage vector in an 18-sector (DTC) flux plane. The proposed control algorithm is comparatively simple and significantly reduces the torque ripple as compared with the basic DTC. Simulation and experimental results proposed algorithm shows the competency of estimator.

articleTitle: A Novel Temperature Invariant Ring Oscillator for Low Power Application
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of Ring Oscillator (RO) with less frequency variation against change in temperature. The proposed RO is driven by threshold voltage dependent supply voltage to achieve lower frequency variation along with low power consumption. As the inverters are the principal components of RO, so different logic styles like CMOS and feed through logic (FTL) is used to design the RO. Simulations are carried out using 180 nm CMOS technology to validate the result.

articleTitle: Primary Review on MPPT Method and Size of Grid Connected Solar Photovoltaic Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In case of grid connected solar photovoltaic inverter, the MPPT technique and size of inverter should be selected carefully. The study in this paper is aimed to address these two major issues subjected with grid connected solar photovoltaic system viz. (i) accurate tracking of maximum power point and (ii) power loss due to use of centralized inverter. Although these both issues are independent of each other, they will result in power loss and reduced output power. The conventional MPPT method suffers from three major problems of continues oscillations around MPP, divergence away from MPP by losing the tracking direction and partial shading. Lot of modified version of MPPT methods are presented by researchers around the globe to address the problem and possible solutions, few of them are discussed in this paper. Still, the advanced MPPT methods are yet to be commercialized. In addition to that, a centralized inverter for large solar photovoltaic power plant has few dis advantages like module mismatch loss, shading losses etc. A module integrated inverter can be the best option to reduce this power loss problem. A comparative analysis of power generation by centralized inverter and module integrated inverter is done for 3.0kWp solar photovoltaic system in PVSyst software.

articleTitle: A Novel Control Scheme for Solar PV Fed PMSM Driven Energy Efficient Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work proposes a single stage standalone solar photovoltaic (PV) array powered water pumping system using a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The presented system includes a PV array, a three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI), a PMSM and a pump. The electrical energy from the solar PV array is fed to the VSI which acts as power processing unit (PPU) and supplies desired currents to drive the PMSM. As the motor rotates, the pump attached to the motor accomplishes the objective of water pumping. The vital contribution of this work includes: (i) development of a novel modified vector control, which improves the torque response of the system, (ii) implementation of single stage variable step size incremental conductance (VSS-INC) technique, which provides a fast peak power point tracking and eliminates the need of intermediate stage and (iii) introduction of solar PV feed forward term, which accelerates the overall performance of the system under dynamic conditions. Behavior of the proposed system is realized through simulation studies using MATLAB/Simulink. Moreover the system performance is also validated experimentally under varying environmental conditions using hardware prototype developed in the laboratory using the digital signal processor DS1102.

articleTitle: Switched-Capacitor-Based Three-Phase Five-Level Inverter Topology With Reduced Components
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new five-level multilevel inverter (MLI) based on retrofitting of the conventional two-level (2L) three-phase inverter modules with minimum structural reconfigurations for low-voltage and high-power-quality demanding applications. It comprises two such inverter modules connected in series with 2L switched-capacitor units (SCUs). It requires only two isolated dc sources which are shared by all inverter output phases and thus eliminates the chances of output phase unbalance. Further, the voltage across the floating capacitors of the SCUs are naturally regulated without any sensors, thus makes the proposed topology more elegant for industrial applications. Further, an extensive comparison with the recent other MLI topologies attests the reduced requirement of the components in devising the proposed topology. Finally, experimental results from a low-power hardware prototype are presented to validate the feasibility of the proposed configuration.

articleTitle: Neuro-Fuzzy Logic Based Control Scheme for PV-Battery Integrated Sensorless Induction Motor Drive for Water Pumping
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper deals with a bidirectional power flow scheme for a PV array-battery interfaced system for an induction motor drive used for water pumping. The bidirectional power flow is achieved by bidirectional buck-boost converter. The motor control is achieved by field-oriented control (FOC), without mechanical sensor. The proposed system uses rotor flux based MRAS (Model Reference Adaptive System), with minimum parameters requirement, which is achieved by neuro-fuzzy based speed estimation technique. The DC link current is sufficient to estimate three phase motor winding currents. The modified space vector modulation technique is used for phase currents estimation. The developed prototype is tested in the laboratory and its suitability is judged through various test results under different conditions of insolation variations and also current sensor failure condition.

articleTitle: Islanding Detection for Grid Connected Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES), the area of solar photovoltaic (PV) system has proficient a significant growth for the previous three decades in its extensive use from standalone to utility communicating PV systems. The finest way to use the power generated by the PV array is to distribute it to the AC grid. When solar PV system is associated to the utility grid, various technical concerns have to be analyzed thoroughly. One of the important phenomenon is islanding condition and this islanding can affect the utility workers as well as destruction of the other part of the system. In this paper, different types of islanding detection techniques for grid connected solar PV system are discussed and comparative analysis is made based on power quality (PQ) effect, cost and others.

articleTitle: Operational Strategy of Energy Storage to Address Day-Ahead Scheduling Errors in High RE Scenario
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: High penetration of intermittent renewable generation may impose supply-demand mismatch in real time operation due to day-ahead forecast errors. This results in increase of cycling from conventional generating unit fleet there by cost of generation increases. To address the issue, this paper presents a MILP based 2- step security constrained scheduling problem considering Day-ahead hourly scheduling and intra hour re-dispatch. Further, benefits of using Energy Storage Systems for balancing and reserve services are evaluated. Effectiveness of proposed model is studied on IEEE-118 test system.

articleTitle: Stacked Benefits of Energy Storage in Microgrid Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: High penetration of intermittent renewable generation and in turn reduced flexibility may lead to frequent system imbalances. This poses real-time operational challenges for system operator and necessitates the deployment of multiple services in different time horizons. With high response rates and energy shifting capabilities, energy storage system can become a pragmatic solution for this. However, the major snag in their proliferation is high investment cost and less return associated with single service. In this context, the paper analyses multiple services of ESS and benefits associated with them. A Mix-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model for day-ahead scheduling in 15 minutes temporal is formulated with an objective of profit maximization of a Microgrid owner. Uncertainty of generation and load is handled using Monte Carlo simulation. Study shows that in a scenario of high renewable penetration, participation of energy storage improves reliability of microgrid and profit is maximum when storage is scheduled for multiple services.

articleTitle: A study on different configurations of fractional order fuzzy logic controller scheme for robotic manipulator using NSGA-II
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, the performance and design analysis of two different configurations of fractional order fuzzy logic controller (FLC) schemes are investigated for two-link planar robotic manipulator plant. The plant under consideration is carrying a payload which is varying with time. The scaling gains of FLC and the other parameters of controller are obtained using an efficient multi-objective optimization technique named as non-dominating sorted genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II). Two different performance/objective functions are chosen for minimization to witness trade-off between them and to obtain better closed loop response. Using the MATLAB/Simulink platform for simulation, the performance of the proposed controller techniques are compared with the fractional version of PID (FOPID) and traditional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller. For the robustness testing, the results for the disturbance rejections are presented for all the control schemes.

articleTitle: Performance of Sensorless Method for PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In AC Drives control of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is a nontrivial matter, due to its nonlinear elements and time-fluctuating parameters. In many industries, PMSM drives require speed/position sensorless operation of high performance. A large portion of the sensorless control scheme is dependent motor parameter. Therefore motor performance suffers much in hostile and highly flactuating operating environment where motor parameter is varying. To defeated this issue, Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) based calculations have been produced, which offer versatile and straightforward solution. The test results exhibit that sensorless PMSM drive display better speed tracking.

articleTitle: Super Twisting SMC Based Speed Sensorless PMSM Driven Solar PV Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a super twisting sliding mode controller based (ST-SMC) vector controlled speed sensorless permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) driven single stage solar photovoltaic (PV) water pumping system is proposed. The ST-SMC minimizes chattering associated with the conventional SMC without affecting tracking accuracy, steady-state performance and robustness of the system. The rotor position is estimated using back-emf method. This eliminates the need of costly mechanical position sensors and increases reliability of the system. A drift free perturb and observe (DF-PO) maximum power point (MPP) tracking (MPPT) algorithm is used to operate solar PV array at MPP. The output of MPPT controller and the DC link ST-SMC are used to generate reference speed command. The switching pulses for voltage source inverter (VSI) are generated by the hysteresis controller. A prototype of the proposed system is developed. The steady-state, starting and dynamic performances are examined under variable solar irradiations.

articleTitle: Dynamic Retail Pricing for Load Serving Entity Under Significant Renewable Energy Penetration
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Renewable energy (RE) penetration has strongly increased in the electricity market worldwide. Variability and availability of RE are challenging load-serving entity's (LSE) decision-making about energy procurement portfolio and retail price offer. The influence of RE penetration on LSE's optimal decisions would increase with penetration level. This necessitates an investigation on LSE's participation strategy in electricity market under significant RE penetration. Besides RE, consumers' flexible demand may negatively affect LSE's decisions and eventually its expected profit. This necessitates dynamic retail pricing to manage flexible demand and exploit monetary benefits from it. In this perspective, this paper presents a model for LSE to determine optimal dynamic retail prices and optimal energy procurement portfolio in the presence of flexible demand and significant RE penetration. A case study is employed to illustrate and validate the proposed model.

articleTitle: Development of Observer-Based Photovoltaic MPP Tracker under Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A new and simple current sensorless particle swarm optimization (PSO) to extract maximum power under partial shading condition in a photovoltaic (PV) power generation system is proposed in this paper. The existing techniques used for extracting the maximum power in a PV system, in partial shading condition, requires the current and voltage sensors. The use of current sensors (CS) for tracking maximum power point in a partial shading condition is completely avoided in the proposed work. This make the system more simple, less cost, easy to implement and reliable. The effectiveness of the proposed method is studied with the help of a suitable simulation carried in MATLAB platform and for experimental validation a microcontroller is used. The results obtained from the simulations and experimental studies showed that the proposed current sensorless method can track the maximum power point accurately, in partial shading conditions.

articleTitle: An Electrically Isolated Low Power LED Driver Offering Power Factor Correction with Ameliorated Mains Current THD
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient design of an electrically isolated low power (12w) light emitting diode (LED) driver with active power factor controller (PFC) based on buck converter topology. The presented system comprises a rectifier-fed-PFC unit which reduces the harmonic distortion of the mains (230V r.m.s.) line current by improving the sending-end power factor. There is a dc-link-inverter which consists of a soft switched buck converter and a parallel-loaded series L-C resonant inverter. At the receiving-end, there is a high frequency transformer provided isolation and a rectifier to feed appropriate voltage and current to a 12w LED lighting load. The switching converters are controlled by pulse width modulation (PWM) signals of 20kHz. The framework has been simulated on PLECS software. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of the mains line current is approximately 10.7904% at 0.9893 sending-end power factor whereas the third harmonic current is 6.1538% and the fifth harmonic current is 5.4557% of the fundamental current and these are less than the recommended values of IEC 61000-3-2. The voltage and current waveforms of every converter stage corroborate the reliability of the proposed work.

articleTitle: Wide-area PMU-ANN based monitoring of low frequency oscillations in a wind integrated power system
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The wind integration is on the rise in modern grids to generate cleaner energy due to increasing environmental concerns. This further escalates the problem of low frequency oscillations (LFOs) in power system. Thus, real-time monitoring of oscillations becomes even more important in present interconnected power systems. The conventional methods are offline and time consuming. In this work, a wide-area based method employing Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is proposed to predict the system oscillatory status in real-time. The PMUs are optimally placed using modified Integer Linear Programming. The PMU data is dimensionally reduced using Principal Component Analysis before using it to train the ANN. The ANN predicts the LFO related information like damping ratio and frequency and an index to access the mode's localness. The proposed methodology is verified on IEEE New England benchmark system. The suggested method is very fast and accurate in predicting the required information in real-time for different operating conditions involving topological variations with very less computational requirement.

articleTitle: A Series Compensated Open-end Winding Induction Generator System for DC loads and AC linear, Non-linear and Unbalanced loads
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a series compensated induction generator system with open-end stator windings for feeding power simultaneously to DC loads and frequency insensitive AC loads including non-linear and unbalanced loads. A two level voltage source inverter (VSI) with a charged capacitor at the DC link has been used to provide the necessary reactive power to the generator as well as the loads. The induction generator supplies only the active power to the loads. The proposed system with DC loads connected across the DC link of the VSI and constant voltage variable frequency loads connected to the AC side has been experimentally verified using an induction generator with open-end stator windings. The behaviour of the system with non-linear and unbalanced loads at AC side has also been experimentally observed. The control scheme was implemented using a digital signal processor – TMS320F28335.

articleTitle: Fault Classification for Single Phase Photovoltaic Systems using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Photovoltaic monitoring is essential in all kinds of systems for its efficient and optimal working. Even after development of modern protection devices, a lot of faults remain undetected. This paper develops a monitoring and detection algorithm for various faults and operating conditions in single phase PV system. The algorithm is developed using wavelet transform and pattern recognition and classification abilities of machine learning techniques. Discrete wavelet transform is used for extracting features of a given signal at pre-processing stage while multi-layer perceptron neural network is used for fault classification process. The data required for developing the algorithm is obtained by simulating PV system for various operating conditions in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The developed algorithm depicts 99.3% training accuracy and 100% testing accuracy for a randomly divided data set.

articleTitle: Control of Induction Motor Drives –Technological Advancements
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The induction motor (IM) with variable frequency AC inverter is widely used in industrial applications which require good dynamic and steady state performance over a wide range of speed. Scalar control has always been inaccurate and gives poor dynamic performance due of the coupling between variables. Vector control by rotor flux orientation drives the machine analogous to a DC machine and offers good dynamic performance for a wide range of application. However, the dynamic performance is dependent over the precise measurement of rotor flux, torque and speed. Direct torque control (DTC) on the other hand reduces the complexity of speed measurement, but requires flux and torque estimation. In this paper, industrial benefits and problems of DTC method has been discussed and reviewed with the latest improved available solutions of such problems. The problem of real time flux estimation over wide range can be overcome by using sensorless control of IM. In this paper estimation techniques of flux magnitude and its position are also reviewed and presented.

articleTitle: Assessment of Energy Storage Potential for Primary Frequency Response Adequacy in Future Grids
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Variable demand pattern with large integration of Renewable Energy Source (RES) would challenge utilities, to ensure inertia and primary frequency response (PFR) adequacy. Displacement of synchronous generators, further results in reduction of system's inherent inertia and PFR capability. This would pose system security and reliability concerns, particularly at the time of contingency like largest generation outage or loss of large chunk of load. These megawatt (MW) imbalances requires an additional response, to make system frequency stable. In view of these issue, this paper assesses potential of energy storage for PFR adequacy in day-ahead generator scheduling problem by simultaneous consideration of operation cost minimization, netload variation and largest generator outage. Simulations are performed on IEEE-118 bus test system with step wise increment in PV and Wind penetration. System inertia quantum, rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) and frequency deviation at nadir is considered as frequency security parameters for the assessment of PFR adequacy. Obtained results presents systematic analysis of energy storage contribution to mitigate PFR requirement at different RES penetration and improvement in frequency nadir. Further, operation cost analysis is presented with variation in RES penetration. This analysis would help system operator to pragmatically handle inevitable system contingencies. This framework could be potentially enhanced to incorporate technologies like, demand response & electric vehicles in future low carbon power system.

articleTitle: Investigation of Weather Influence in Day-Ahead Hourly Electric Load Power Forecasting with New Architecture Realized in Multivariate Linear Regression & Artificial Neural Network Techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In a liberalized deregulated environment, Electric Load Power Forecasting (ELPF) is an important process in any power system network to make it an efficient, secure and customer friendly network. The proposed day-ahead ELPF models are built on a new multiple parallel inputs and output architecture with selected calendar, weather and lagged load power features. In these, the calendar and lagged load power features are kept as constants and weather as a variable feature so that influence of weather on accuracy of day-ahead ELPF can be investigated by different combinational selection of weather variables. The real time data used for this research work were collected from Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited (TPDDL). The models are developed using both multivariate linear regression (MvLR) and feed forward back propagation artificial neural network (ANN) techniques which are implemented using Matlab programming environment. The performance evaluation criteria for ELPF are presented with determination of various statistical errors. The performance of each model is analyzed and the results are presented. The proposed models yield an average forecast error of 2.9% to 3.5% for day-ahead hourly forecast, throughout the year, irrespective of variations in weather. The proposed day-ahead ELPF models are evident for its simplicity, less measurement requirement and easiness in implementation with higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of STATCOM using Improved Sine Cosine Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: As the power system continuously operates under stressed condition due to various constraints, i.e. economic, right of way and regulations etc. FACTS devices are used to provide flexible control of the power systems. STATCOM is used to control the various parameters of the power system either by injecting or absorbing the reactive power but subjected to the cost. Therefore, this paper concerns with the optimal number, location and size of holomorphic embedded load-flow (HELF) model of STATCOM in the multi-bus power systems using improved sine cosine optimization algorithm (ISCA). The IEEE 30-bus test system is considered to validate the algorithm for optimal allocation of HELF model. The results are also compared with the sine-cosine algorithm (SCA) and grey wolf optimization (GWO).

articleTitle: Single-Phase Grid Interfaced Hybrid Solar PV and Wind System using STF-FLL for Power Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a self-tuning filter-frequency locked loop (STF-FLL) based control algorithm is proposed for power quality improvement in single phase utility grid integrated to solar photovoltaic (PV) array with a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based wind energy generation system (WEGS). The STF-FLL control is designed for effective extraction of fundamental components of load current. The proposed technique offers a high degree of insensitivity and immunity to power disturbances. The main objective of the system, is to supply active power to the load and a single phase grid, connected at point of common coupling (PCC). Moreover, it also mitigates the power quality issues like grid current harmonics distortion and provides load reactive power compensation. The grid connected voltage source converter (VSC) acts as a distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) in the absence of power from the PV array as well as from the wind turbine and improves the power quality of the current drawn from the grid. The STF-FLL technique extracts the fundamental components of the grid voltage for grid synchronization. To achieve maximum power, a perturb and observe (P&O) based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm is used. A feed-forward term for solar and wind contribution, is introduced for improving the dynamic response for the changes in solar insolation and wind speed, respectively. The implementation of proposed control is simple and the system response is fast. The behavior of system is tested under dynamic loading, variable solar insolation and changing wind speed conditions on a developed prototype in the laboratory. The performances of proposed system satisfy the objective the proposed scheme and the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Improved Dual Battery Charging System for Grid Connected Bi-directional EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an isolated low power bidirectional on board electric vehicle (EV) dual battery charging topology with grid connectivity and unity power factor (UPF) operation. The proposed EV charging system is able to exchange active and reactive power demand by either side of the bidirectional charger. The primary EV battery operates in a bidirectional charging mode through a dual active bridge converter with a phase shifting operation whereas the auxiliary battery operates in a unidirectional mode to provide power to the EV auxiliary units. This improved topology of dual battery charging system operates independently to maintain necessary amount of battery voltage without affecting the transformer efficiency. The active and reactive power demand is met by the high capacity EV primary battery, whereas the auxiliary battery is intended only for unidirectional controlled power flow. In this paper the EV charging topology is investigated with a front end decoupled power control and a secondary battery sliding mode control (SMC) for bi-directional power flow operation. The mathematical model of the proposed converter is discussed through state space averaging technique to analyse the converter dynamics with variable demand during bi-directional power flow operation. A MATLAB and Simulink is used to develop the proposed circuit topology of dual battery EV charging system for a 4kW single phase grid connected system. The prototype is designed to validate the DC-DC power flow with a high frequency isolation.

articleTitle: Inertia and Primary Frequency Response Assessment Under Uncertain Photovoltaic Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Increasing generation share from uncertain photovoltaic (PV) generation necessitates an assessment of inertia and primary frequency response (PFR) for the reliable and secure power system operations. As large PV integration would cater formidable operational issue for the system operator (SO) to deliver inertia and PFR, particularly at the time of contingency like largest generation outage. Hence, this FR assessment is imperative component for low carbon power system operations. In this perspective, this paper proposes an exposition of FR constrained stochastic generation scheduling model for minimization of operation cost with simultaneous characterization of PV generation uncertainty. Scenario generation and reduction technique is used for pragmatic modelling of PV uncertainty. Proposed model is assessed on one area IEEE RTS for estimation of system inertia and PFR adequacy. Results demonstrate FR ability of the proposed exposition in terms of frequency security parameters like rate of change of frequency (ROCOF), frequency deviation and FR index.

articleTitle: Natural Genetics Adapted Control for an Autonomous Wind-Battery Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a natural genetics and evolution based control strategy for adjusting the gains of the proportional and integral (PI) controller meant for regulating the speed of the generator of an autonomous microgrid system using wind energy generation and a battery energy storage (BES). The variable wind speed operation leads to the dereliction of the fixed gain PI controller as it is sensitive to parameter variations and load disturbances. The genetic algorithm (GA) is implemented for adapting the gains of PI controller according to the changing operating conditions. It avoids the entrapments of the optimal solution in the local search space. The optimal solution is selected on the basis of best fit candidate. The synchronous generator (SG) reference speed is obtained using perturb and observe (P&O) maximum power extraction scheme. The flexible power flow control is obtained using a BES with a bidirectional converter. A prototype of the microgrid is developed in the laboratory and tested in accordance to the IEEE-519 standard under steady state and dynamic conditions including variable wind speeds and load removal.

articleTitle: Cloud Energy Storage Management System with Price Fluctuations and Distributed Generation Intermittency
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The fluctuations of electricity prices in demand response schemes and intermittency of renewable energy supplies necessitate the adoption of energy storage in power systems. These energy storage system require some management strategies to deliver energy optimally in the presence of intermittent behavior of the renewable generation and the dynamic nature of electricity price. This paper presents a cost minimization algorithm based on arbitrary threshold price to charge and discharge the energy storage devices in an optimal way to reduce the electricity cost. This considers distributed generation such as photo-voltaic (PV) generation (domestic rooftop solar and commercial rooftop solar) with cloud energy storage (CES) which reduces the electricity cost by charging the energy storage devices at a negligible price when compared with conventional sources. The simulation results based on load, "domestic and commercial photovoltaic generation'', "wholesale electricity prices of small and medium consumers" for the case study show the feasibility of the proposed approach algorithm for CES management system for cost minimization.

articleTitle: State-of-Art on Flexibility Services in Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Variability and uncertainty due to increased renewable penetration and dynamic role of consumers at distribution end pose operational challenges and generation-demand imbalances for power systems. Ultra-fast response and ramping services to cope up with these uncertainty and variability is a need of forthcoming power system. For operational reliability and grid stability, flexibility resources such as rapid responding generation, demand response, storage and interconnections are identified solutions. Moreover, integrating them with existing power system enhance overall operational and planning costs. Appropriate market products can encourage and incentivize flexibility services. To acquire flexibility services for utilization at different time scales, various markets have adopted various practices according to their system conditions. This paper gives an overview of various country practices of flexibility procurement. A comparative study on flexibility services and market products of various international markets has been carried out to widen understanding about system flexibility services and relevant market products.

articleTitle: Integrated TOU Price-Based Demand Response and Dynamic G2V Charge Scheduling of Electric Vehicle Aggregator
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Electric Vehicle Aggregator (EVA) performs load scheduling coordination for mutual benefits of EV owners and System Operator (SO) under unidirectional grid-to-vehicle (G2V) framework. It performs trading in wholesale markets aiming at profit maximization with buy bids for charging energy requirements and sale bids of regulation services to SO. However, due to unexpected departure of EVs, EVA may incur a loss in trading due to failure in satisfying the charging requirements of EV owners or regulation capacity to SO. It necessitates consideration of a more realistic and flexible smart charge scheduling method for EVs. Furthermore, Time-of-Use price-based demand response (TOU-PBDR) has the potential to enhance economic efficiency of the system through the enhanced flexibility of EVs and incentivize EV owners. In this paper integrated TOU-PBDR and dynamic charge scheduling of EVA is modeled to provide regulation services to SO. Complete charging profile information such as arrival time, departure time, initial SOC, desired SOC, charging efficiency, trip duration, and distance, etc. is not known to EVA antecedently. Simulations are performed on a group of 1000 EVs. Results show fascinating propensities regarding modulation of charging rate, grid stability, and the financial prudence of EV charging.

articleTitle: A Singular Spectrum Analysis based Approach to Price Forecasting for a Day Ahead Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Deregulation across various electricity markets created a need for an operational framework that has capability to run similar to the dynamics of real world commodity markets possessing the competitiveness to ensure long run stability, providing opportunity to every participant and maintaining the price level of commodity within the reach of consumer. The electricity framework takes into account the power system balancing constraints required to ensure its reliability and security. This complex structure with its aim of competitiveness motivated the participating entities to run the generating capacities at the optimum level, forced the operators to minimize the transmission losses and created an environment for the consumers to take the benefit of variable pricing conditions. Specially, these effects are reflected via short term electricity price forecasting (STPF) in a significant amount. The STPF created the required decision base for the entities to bid in market with an effective strategy of risk management to hedge against the highly volatile pricing events to ensure the required amount of liquidity and making better economic conditions while in case of large consumers, it helps to either curtail or schedule the loads to minimize the cost of energy. It also helps them to prepare an alternative strategy to make available the required energy via small private generating units during peak price hours. To account for different requirements of various entities, accurate price forecasting is a crucial task. The complexity of the price dynamics also involves the variations attributed to spatial effects in different operating regions such as calamities and extreme conditions. In this paper, Singular Spectrum Analysis based model is used to forecast the price. The simulations results show the accuracy of proposed model.

articleTitle: Backward/Forward Method for Three-phase Power Flow Calculation in Low Voltage Distribution Networks with EV Charging Points
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper presents comprehensive review on power flow methods, and proposed a robust and fast power flow calculation approach for low voltage three-phase balanced/unbalanced distribution networks considering the Electric Vehicles (EVs) charging points. The proposed approach adopts the Kirchhoff's current law (KCL) and Kirchhoff's voltage law (KVL) to determine the branch currents and node voltages. For fast calculations, a backward/forward sweep approach is adopted to update the bus voltages in each iteration. The individual mathematical modelling of distribution system components are presented. To validate the method, simulation results obtained are compared with existing methods. Further, voltage and loss sensitivities are used to determine the potential charging points and their sizes by considering percentage unbalancing of the system.

articleTitle: An Online Adaptive Intelligent Framework for Customer Willingness Interpretation in Demand Response Exchange
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The demand response exchange presents an independent pool based market clearing mechanism dedicated for resources in the demand side. The active demand resources participate in the pool acting as demand response buyers. The of such buyers can be better represented by utilizing the concepts of fuzzy systems. This paper presents a methodology to enhance the benefit of DR sellers and buyers in the demand response exchange through fuzzy inference system. However, the performance of the fuzzy system is dependent on the structure of membership function and rule base. Thus, an adaptive way of membership function tuning has been adopted in this paper. The tuning of the parameters has been performed using various heuristic approaches to observe the performance of tuned fuzzy system for DRX application compared to traditional non- fuzzy and un-tuned models. The simulation experiments carried out with different load types in different seasons demonstrate the improvement in DRX welfare for adaptively tuned fuzzy system to the traditional and un-tuned models. The adaptive tuning presented in this paper can be used by individual DR seller to calculate the participation bids.

articleTitle: Simulation of Dynamic Inductive Wireless Charging Using Overhead Line
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This study reviews the wireless power transfer (WPT) principles and focuses on the inductive wireless power transfer technique. The concept behind the WPT is thoroughly studied and proper simulations concerning its mechanism of operation have been conducted. Significant attention was given to the WPT using overhead high voltage power line (HVPL). The studied concept implies that the energy is extracted from the HVPL using energy harvesting device and that it is transferred to the consuming device via the magnetically coupled transmitting and receiving coils. Simulations have demonstrated that the energy transferring efficiency and transmission stability are dependent on the frequency at which the power is transferred. While the energy transferring efficiency and the frequency are directly proportional, transmission stability and the frequency reveal inverse proportionality. Another simulation was conducted to investigate the relation between the distance and efficiency. The obtained plots revealed that as the distance increases, the voltage of the overhead line declines drastically.

articleTitle: Application of Intelligent Grey Wolf Optimizer for Transient Stability Constrained Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Due to deregulation in the energy market and rapid increase in the power demand, the power system components are working closely to their permissible limits. Under this environment, the systems' stability and security are the major concern for the system operator. Transient stability and security constrained optimal power flow (TSSCOPF) problem can be developed by employing with OPF line loading and rotor angle trajectory constraints. This paper employs a newly developed variant of GWO named as Intelligent Grey Wolf Optimizer (IGWO) to solve TSSCOPF problem. The application of IGWO has been investigated on TSSCOPF problem for IEEE-30 test bus system. After observing the results and rotor angle trajectories under different severe contingencies, it can be stated that the proposed method is suitable for TSSCOPF problem. Further, the comparison of this variant with some recently published approaches is also presented. The promising results establish the efficacy of IGWO for solving TSSCOPF problem.

articleTitle: PV and TEG Hybrid Power Generation for Enhancement of Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper explores the enhancement of solar module efficiency using hybrid generation from the thermoelectric generator and the photovoltaic cell. The solar energy is in the form of light and heat. Photovoltaic panel absorbs energy from the light particle and assembled thermoelectric generator system generates electrical energy from heat particle. The electricity generation is done due to thermoelectric effect and greenhouse effect of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. This module is designed in such a manner that it makes the system compact and very effective in rooftop of building. Monocrystalline cell and multijunction solar cell are considered for the simulation work keeping in view the scope of technology required in the current and future scenario. This simulation is done using MATLAB/Simulink platform. Proposed design increases the Power efficiency by 10.74% and 20.79% for monocrystalline and multijunction compare to the conventional solar power generation technology. The concept is implemented by combining both layers of generation, which provides more electrical energy compared to the separate layers generation. In this paper, optimal positioning of the light intensity with the panel is utilized to generate maximum energy output.

articleTitle: Coordinating Bidding Strategy of Profit Maximization for Competitive Power Suppliers in Energy and Reserve Markets
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Modern electricity market operates as an oligopolis-tic entity. The power producers earn by supplying power to a local geographical area and providing the ancillary services to the Independent System Operator (ISO). The market imperfection enables the power producer to maximize its profit by unified strategic bidding of both power and ancillary services. Therefore, a suitable bidding strategy is indispensible for power suppliers in the energy and reserve services market. In this paper, the coordinated bidding strategy for competitive power suppliers in an energy and reserve market has been solved using Extended Gravitational Search Algorithm (EGSA). EGSA is based on the notion of oppositional learning where an equal number but opposite agents are generated in the initial search space. The size of search space reduces to half in every iteration based the proximity of solution to an agent or its opposite agent. The proposed method is tested on a test system with six suppliers and results are compared with Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA) and Refined Genetic Algorithm (RGA) previously reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Smart Inverter Functionality for Facilitating Higher Solar PV Penetration in Distribution Feeders
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Rooftop solar photovoltaic installations have grown rapidly across India. Their integration with the local distribution networks may throw some operational challenges with increasing penetration levels. Voltage rise or unbalance and reverse power flows are some of the anticipated concerns. The current grid-connectivity regulations in India only encourage unity power factor operation of solar photovoltaic inverters although reactive power support features are available in commercial models. However, with increasing solar power into the distribution network, smart inverter functionality will assume importance. This paper analyzes the effect of Volt-VAr control mode of solar photovoltaic inverters in providing localized voltage control and reducing reverse power flow. An actual feeder of a distribution utility in Kolkata, West Bengal, India has been extensively modeled and distribution load flow studies have been performed. The preliminary results of this modeling exercise have shown encouraging results in simulation, in support of smart inverter functionality. The need for modeling distribution networks in greater detail beyond the distribution transformer secondary has also been established in order to have a realistic assessment of the impacts of integration of rooftop solar systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Wind Power Effects on Environmental/Economic Load Dispatch Problem by an Intelligent Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Due to the increasing renewable energy sources penetration in the electric power systems and growing concerns about the environmental problems, power network operators attempt to evaluate the optimal economic dispatch of the units. This work proposes a new optimization algorithm named Environmental Economic Dispatch (EED), which aims to solve the multi-objective problem by evaluating wind power impacts on the power system. Thus, the penetration rate of the thermal and wind units will be balanced to minimize the costs. In order to demonstrate the capabilities of the proposed technique, different test scenarios have been considered. By comparing the results with the ones obtained using other techniques, the superiority and validity of the proposed technique is proven.

articleTitle: Riemann-Liouville Operator Based FNLMS Algorithm for 3 Phase- 4 Wire SyRG-PV-BES Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper deals with one three phase voltage source converter (VSC) integrated with renewable energy sources (RESs) such as photovoltaic (PV) array and pico-hydro turbine driven by synchronous reluctance generator (SyRG). The proposed VSC controller is a Riemann-Liouvilla operator centered fractional normalised least mean square (FNLMS) algorithm, which accomplishes improved convergence, flexibility in parameter tuning and steady state performance. The VSC control algorithm in addition, provides harmonics compensation by inserting harmonics current in reverse direction into the system and neutral current compensation to maintain balance in supply. Moreover, in three-phase four wire based microgrid, a bidirectional converter (BDC) is used to harness power from the sources by controlling charging and discharging of the battery. However, the SyRG is used for pico-hydro generation because of its reliability, and cost-effectiveness. The proposed microgrid is implemented in real time using modular DSP (d-SPACE 1006) control. Test results of proposed microgrid, show that the voltage and frequency of microgrid is maintained constant while the system is following a sudden change in loads and under intermittent penetration of solar energy source.

articleTitle: Indirect Current Control of Single-stage Grid-tied Photvoltaic using PSO Assisted PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Single stage inverter handles both maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and active/reactive power control. Synchronous reference frame based dq control philosophy is used for controlling the active and reactive power demand of the local load on distribution side. The current loop controls the inverter current for transferring power to the load/grid at unity power factor. However, voltage loop controls the DC-link voltage which provides the reference current in terms of power loss to the current loop for inverter current calculations. The reference voltage for DC-link control is provided by incremental conductance based MPPT control under variable insolation and temperature. In single stage grid-tied system the reference voltage is floating in nature and the DC-link is maintained constant with proper gain scheduling using particle swarm optimization under varying insolation and load changing conditions. The proposed grid-tied system is simulated in MATLAB Simulink environment and a wide verity of simulation and experimental results are depicted for showing robustness of controller. Grid currents are sinusoidal and well within the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Modelling & Steady State Compliance Testing of an Improved Time Synchronized Phasor Measurement Unit Based on IEEE Standard C37.118.1
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Synchrophasor technology is an emerging and developing technology for monitoring and control of wide area measurement systems (WAMS). In an elementary WAMS, two identical phasors measured at two different locations have difference in the phase angles measured since their reference waveforms are not synchronized with each other. Phasor measurement units (PMUs) measure input phasors with respect to a common reference wave based on the atomic clock pulses received from global positioning system (GPS) satellites, eliminating variation in the measured phase angles due to distant locations of the measurement nodes. This has found tremendous applications in quick fault detection, fault location analysis, accurate current, voltage, frequency and phase angle measurements in WAMS. Commercially available PMU models are often proven to be expensive for research and development as well as for grid integration projects. This research article proposes an economic PMU model optimized for accurate steady-state performance based on recursive discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and provides results and detailed analysis of the proposed PMU model as per the steady state compliance specifications of IEEE standard C37.118.1. Results accurate up to 13 digits after decimal point are obtained through the developed PMU model for both nominal and off-nominal frequency inputs in steady state.

articleTitle: Utility Integrated Variable Speed Wind Energy Conversion System Using Innovation Sequence based Modified Kalman Type Estimator and Improved Robust Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A utility integrated wind energy conversion system (WECS) encounters challenges in regulating the power flow of the grid and peak wind power extraction from the variable speed wind turbine. To take care of these challenges, this paper proposes an innovation sequence based modified Kalman type estimator (ISMKE) based control for the utility side converter (USC) and an improved robust speed control technique with disturbance rejection capability for the wind turbine side converter (WTSC). The proposed ISMKE estimates fundamental positive sequence component from harmonics contaminated nonlinear load current to generate sinusoidal reference grid currents. Estimation of the harmonics and disturbance free positive sequence load currents, is performed for achieving good grid synchronization and load compensation. The USC with proposed control technique is proficient of dealing with the power quality issues such as load unbalancing, power factor correction, harmonics elimination and load compensation. Moreover, it effectively regulates the active power flow from the WECS to the grid. The WTSC uses field oriented control (FOC) that controls the q-axis current, where the reference q-axis current is generated by using the proposed improved robust sliding mode speed control technique that provides improved performance against model uncertainties and external disturbances.

Author Keywords: Utility Integrated Wind Energy Conversion System

articleTitle: A Carrier based PWM Scheme for Dual Inverter-fed Open-end Winding Induction Motor with Single DC Source
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A carrier based pulse width modulation (PWM) scheme for elimination of common mode voltages (CMV) from the windings of a dual-inverter fed induction motor (IM) with open-end stator windings is presented in this paper. One of the main features of this PWM scheme is the prevention of flow of common-mode (CM) currents that facilitates use of single DC voltage source to power both inverters. This method is simpler compared to the conventional SVPWM techniques for dual inverter fed drives as it does not involve complex procedures like sector identification and dwell-time calculations. Validation of this scheme is done by extensive simulation and experiment on a laboratory proto-type.

articleTitle: Recursive Digital Filter Based Control for Power Quality Improvement of Grid Tied Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The proposed work deals with the implementation of a control approach for an active power transfer between solar photovoltaic (PV) array and grid/ load alongwith power quality improvement by eliminating harmonics and compensating reactive power required by the load in the distribution system. The PV array is directly connected across the DC link of a voltage source converter (VSC). The power is transferred to the grid/ load through VSC, which performs the function of distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) by injecting compensating currents in the proposed system. The PV array is operated at maximum power by employing the usage of perturb and observe (P&O) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) approach in order to extract the available maximum power from the solar PV array. A feed-forward term for the solar PV array power, is incorporated for the enhancement of dynamic response. The prominence of the control algorithm lies in the efficient switching of VSC, by generating reference grid currents, which are obtained through indirect current control technique. The recursive digital filter is utilized for processing the load currents and extracting the active power component of the load currents. Therefore, the active power component of load currents obtained, are used for generating the reference grid currents in the proposed system. A prototype of the system is developed in the laboratory and its performance is studied for varying loads, changing solar insolation, and voltage swell and voltage sag conditions.

articleTitle: Unit commitment in thermal power generation dispatching with integration of PHEVs
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, presents a novel approach metaheuristics algorithm quasi oppositional passing vehicle search (QOPVS) algorithm for solve the unit commitment problem (UCP) of thermal units integrated with plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) in an electrical power system to optimize specific fuel consumption (FC) and emissions. Passing vehicle search (PVS) algorithm is a population based algorithm which mechanism is inspired by passing vehicles on two-lane rural highways. As algorithms are population based so enables to provide improved solution with integration of powerful techniques. A powerful technique named opposite based learning techniques (OBLT) is integrated with proposed PVS algorithm. OBLT provides enough strength to proposed PVS algorithm to gain a better approximation for both current and opposite population at the same time, as it provide a solution which is more nearer solution from optimal based from starting by checking both solutions. Thermal unit scheduling with PHEV problem is a nonlinear, nonconvex, discrete, complex and constrained optimization problem. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed QOPVS algorithm, an IEEE 10-unit test system is employed to investigate the impacts of PHEVs on generation scheduling. The results obtained from simulation analysis show a significant techno-economic saving.

Author Keywords: Quasi Oppositional Passing Vehicle Search Algorithm

articleTitle: Decentralized PEVs Energy Management Scheme for Supplementary Frequency Regulation Considering Mobility Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Need of reduction in CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions and increased oil demand in automobile sector resulted in development of Plugin Electric Vehicles (PEVs). It has a rechargeable battery and can act as storage device. This mobile battery storage device is utilised to implement Vehicle 2 Grid (V2G) technology. In this paper, the mathematical model has been suggested to serve the grid in term of ancillary service such as frequency regulation. The regulation signal from PJM is used to simulate the proposed scheme. To meet the regulation signal effectively, thousands of PEVs have to participate in this scheme. So, the idea of the aggregator is integrated into the proposed scheme to control the fleets of PEVs. The regulation signal is used to determine the total charging and discharging power of PEVs to regulate the frequency. The results show the proposed scheme is able to meet the high negative regulation signal with G2V action due to availability of PEVs for charging. But it fails to perform properly during high positive regulation signal with V2G action due to unavailability of PEVs for discharging. The arrival of PEVs at the Charging Station (CS) is governed by mobility data of Korean Transportation Safety Authority.

articleTitle: An Asymmetric Seven Level Multilevel Converter for Grid Integrated Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The presented work deals with an asymmetric seven level cascaded configuration for solar photovoltaic (PV) grid integrated system, which contains two H-bridges with asymmetric DC link voltages i.e. unequal DC link voltage. It helps to enhance the output voltage levels that is controlled at V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> for H-bridge1 and 2V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> for H-bridge2 making it as 1:2 ratio for binary voltage values and attains seven level as its output voltage. Level shifted pulse width modulation (LS-PWM) technique is used to provide pulses to the respective switches of the insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBT). Reduced switching frequency is the major attribute for the system. Power quality issues are also dealt with case in order to provide better performance for the desired system configuration within IEEE-519 and IEEE-719 standards.

Author Keywords: Asymmetric seven level cascaded multilevel converter

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of PMSG for Wind Turbine Using Optimum Torque Control and D-Axis Current Control
