publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work propose a approach for improving performance of a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) with uncertain wind velocity. In this work, a maximum power point tracing (MPPT) approach control the optimum torque of the PMSG with respect to wind speed and direct-axis current controller reduces the winding losses of generator. The electromagnet torque of the PMSG is correlated with the magnitude of the quadric-axis current, while the direct-axis current is zero. The performance of the proposed MPPT method and direct-axis current controller of PMSG incorporating loss minimization and improving efficiency is simulation result at variable wind speed conditions. The proposed control strategy is implemented in MATLAB software.

articleTitle: Average Model of Isolated Bidirectional DC-DC Converter with Auxiliary Isolated Clamp
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Dual active bridge converter is one of the examples for nonlinear time-varying system. This paper narrates mathematical model of bidirectional converter with the galvanic isolation. The control-to-output transfer function has been established with the help of state space average method for both modes of operation. The nonlinear mathematical model has been converted to a linear model by state space average method. The open loop transfer function has been derived for both the mode of operations. The compensation has been subjected to an open loop system. The PI parameters were adjusted from the state space analysis. The effectiveness of the proposed converter is verified with the help of the simulation tool PSIM. Bode plot has been plotted to verify the stability of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Nonadaptive CDSC Based Control of a Single Phase PV System Tied to Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The nonadaptive cascaded delayed signal cancellation (CDSC) based control algorithm is proposed for a double stage photovoltaic (PV) system tied to the distribution grid. The proposed control algorithm uses five αβDSC operators in cascade with delay factors of 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 to filter out double frequency oscillation, to ensure a 90° phase difference between it’s α- axis and β-axis outputs, and mitigates all odd harmonics under both nominal and off-nominal frequencies to ensure accurate fundamental component of load current tracking. This control has good DC offset rejection. This control technique extracts active component of load current, to generate sinusoidal reference grid current. The PV system to DSTATCOM (Distribution Static Compensator) mode, and DSTATCOM to PV system operation, besides injecting active power to the grid, is demonstrated through test results. The total harmonic distortion (THD) in grid current is attained within the compliance of distribution grid code as imposed by the IEEE-929 and 519 PQ (Power Quality) standards.

articleTitle: A Modified Duty Cycle Frequency Control Soft Switching of Full Bridge DC-DC Converter for Electric Vehicle Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The choice of an efficient dc-dc converter plays an important role in the its designing and switching. In this paper, modified duty cycle frequency control (MDFC) is discussed. The converter parameter design is also discussed. In the MDFC method, the APWM is combined with variable operating switching frequency. The optimal control of the switching frequency controls the peak current of the auxiliary inductors with loosing the soft switching during transition period of the switches. Therefore, the efficiency of the converter increases by reducing the switching loss, conduction loss, circulating loss and auxiliary circuit loss with the help of the proposed modified control for 1.2 KW system.

articleTitle: An Efficient Wireless Topology for Electric Vehicle Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A choice of high frequency power converter topology plays an important role in the battery charging of electric vehicles (EVs). Inductive power transfer (IPT) systems is more convenient and safer over conventional plug-in systems to charge the battery pack of EVs. Available IPT system can utilizes either zero voltage switching (ZVS) or zero current switching (ZCS) while maintaining sinusoidal power shape. While achieving ZVS and ZCS for all power switches simultaneously is a challenging task in wireless power transfer. The improvement of efficiency is done by utilizing ZCS and ZVS together at the cost of losing sinusoidal power shape and derating of system. In this paper an improved zero-voltage zerocurrent switching (ZVZCS) WPT topology is proposed. The soft switching for the converter switches is achieved with classical series compensation. The efficiency of converter is improved form its conventional topology. The simulation is done using MATLAB/SIMULINK for 1.2 kW load.

articleTitle: Planning of Fast Charging Stations in Distribution System Coupled with Transportation Network for Capturing EV flow
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Promotion of Electric Vehicles (EVs) over conventional vehicles due to environmental concern calls for the optimal location and sizing of Fast Charging Stations (FCS) to facilitate the large-scale EV deployment. EV FCS couple future transportation networks and power systems. That is EV driving and charging behavior will influence both the networks. This paper proposes optimal location and sizing of FCS which ensures maximal capture of EV flow and reduced investment cost by minimizing the number of charging facilities required in the FCS. A battery capacity constrained EV flow capturing location model to maximize the EV traffic flow is proposed. Further queuing analysis based waiting time constrained sizing model is proposed to minimize the number of charging facilities in an FCS. This is a Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) problem solved by the two variants of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) technique. The simulation is conducted on a case study consisting of 123-bus distribution system and a 25-node traffic network system to illustrate the proposed planning method. The impact of different load models of FCS for power flow analysis on the distribution system is also studied.

articleTitle: Hybrid Space Vector Modulation Scheme for Dual Inverter Fed Open End Winding Induction Motor Drive for Improved Harmonic Distortion
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid space vector modulation (SVM) scheme with reduced harmonic ripple for a dual inverter fed open end winding induction motor (OEWIM) for various fundamental frequencies and operating power factors is presented. Various SVM methods are compared based on the harmonic distortion to identify the zones of superior performance and to propose a hybrid SVM for the entire operating range. In dual inverter fed OEWIM drives, the reference voltage can be synthesized by level shifted carrier based SVM method or by using decoupled SVM method. In the decoupled SVM method, each inverter can be switched independently of each other, thus different SVM techniques can be applied in the individual inverter. This paper exploits the above possibility and analyses combinations of conventional SVM and bus clamping SVM applied to the individual inverters in terms of their harmonic performance. Harmonic performance of various SVM techniques are compared using the concept of stator current ripple and is analysed for various fundamental frequencies and operating power factors to find an optimum method over the entire modulation range. The SVM methods are analysed using MATLAB Simulink by operating an induction motor drive under open-loop volts per hertz control scheme with fixed number of samples per fundamental frequency.

articleTitle: A Direct Torque Control Scheme for Five-phase Induction Motor Drive with Reduced Current Distortion
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Direct torque control (DTC) is one of the most widely used control strategy in induction motor drives. DTC drive utilizes the hysteresis band control which is one of the simplest and popular control scheme. The major problems in the conventional DTC scheme is large torque ripple, stator current distortion and variable switching frequency. This paper presents a DTC scheme for five phase induction motor drive to achieve constant switching frquency and minimum distortion in the stator current. The proposed DTC scheme is validated by extensive simulation on a Matlab-Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Investigation of Power Quality in Power Distribution System using Real-time Simulator
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) provides active and reactive powers to enable harmonic current elimination, voltage and frequency mitigation, load compensation, and flicker mitigation. In this paper, investigation on power quality improvement in the presence of non linear and unbalanced load is done. The control algorithm provided for DSTAT-COM is p-q algorithm, anti-hebbian algorithm, and Synchronous reference frame algorithm. Comparison among various control algorithm is done on the basis of performance under non-linear and unbalanced load, Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), dynamic performance, complexity and reactive power compensation. The study has been carried out using real time simulator OPAL-RT. OP4510 is used for analysis and validation of results.

articleTitle: Multipulse Diode Rectifiers: Power Quality Perspective Based On Experimental Data
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The diode rectifiers are essentially uncontrolled, unidirectional ac-dc converters that provide dc output voltage. Power diodes that constitute these converters have the largest voltage, current and hence, power dissipation ratings compared with the other semiconductor devices including the self-latching and self-commutating ones. Single- and three-phase topologies of these converters cater to a plethora of applications that range from a few milliwatts to several megawatts. In this paper the diode rectifiers have been classified into three types, the fundamental ones that have a pulse number less than or equal to three and the multipulse ones that can be realized by the series or parallel cascade of the former, to facilitate analysis from the power quality viewpoint. The advantages of the multipulse diode rectifiers and their capability of ac to dc conversion in compliance with current power quality standards are experimentally verified. In this paper, the power quality data of various rectifier topologies obtained from prototypes have been analyzed to establish correlation of the pulse number with performance parameters. Topologies of the single-, two-, three-, six-, twelve- and eighteen-pulse rectifiers and their power quality indices obtained from experimental data are presented.

articleTitle: Current Mirror Circuit Based Low Cost Lead Acid Battery Charger for Solar PV
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel current mirror circuit based low cost lead acid battery charger for standalone solar PV system. The charging operation is automatically adjusted by combination of voltage regulator and current mirror circuit. Current mirror circuit is designed to carry larger current for fast charging of battery where voltage regulator maintains a constant voltage. This work has been started considering a 12 volt 100 Ah Lead Acid Battery at c/10. Simulation of the battery charger has been analyzed in NI MULTISIM 14. Hardware and simulated results of the proposed prototype 100 Ah charger with solar PV shows reliable operation.

articleTitle: Application of FGMOS Based Wilson Current Mirror in Transimpedance Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A new high gain wideband CMOS transimpedance amplifier (TIA) is designed which is suitable for low-power low-voltage applications. The main aim of this paper is to increase the gain of TIA with reduced supply requirement and for this, floating gate metal oxide semiconductor (FGMOS) based Wilson current mirror (WCM) is used. Small signal analysis is also done to show the bandwidth enhancement. Simulation results of proposed TIA show the transimpedance gain of 56.8dBΩ which is about 5.7 dBΩ greater than simple TIA and the bandwidth of 5GHz with 0.58mW from 1V power supply.

articleTitle: Modeling and Investigation of Insulation Defects by Partial Discharge in HV XLPE Cable
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) analysis is a reliable diagnostic tool to assess the integrity and the quality of electrical insulation of power systems. Cable, insulator, bushing, power transformer, and other related parts of electrical equipment are used in the power system network. Spherical void in the insulation of the high voltage cable is assumed as origin of partial discharge (PD) and it may lead to heavy damage to the insulating system. This paper presents experimental PD test measurements as a function of void size, applied voltage and three capacitor type models for partial discharge simulation using MATLAB Simulink for 11 kV cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable with void by implementing the standard PD model. For detection the imperfect XLPE insulation, the partial discharge detection method is used. The initiation of PD pulses in 11kV high voltage XLPE cable is presented with charge waveform and resulting PD pulses.

articleTitle: Solar PV Based DC Microgrid under Partial Shading Condition with Battery-Part 1: Maximum Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation depends on the solar irradiation level and temperature. The modules of solar PV array receive different solar irradiations under partial shading conditions (PSCs). Therefore multiple of local maxima and a global maxima power point achieve in the power-voltage characteristics of the solar array. The effects of system variables such as series resistance, parallel resistance, different solar array configurations, and different shading patterns on solar PV power generation are discussed. To increase the maximum power generation from solar PV array different topologies of the PV module connection can be used. In this paper the series-parallel (SP) and total cross tied (TCT) configurations are considered. The effect of parallel connected bypass diodes with each PV module is analyzed. Different system variables are discussed to enhance the overall efficiency of the solar PV array. The analytical results are presented using MATLAB software.

articleTitle: IAE and ISE Performance Criterion Based Loop Filter Tuning of Transport Delay-Phase Locked Loop (TD-PLL) for Single Phase Grid Connected Inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Transport delay based Phase Locked Loop (TD-PLL) algorithm has gained wide acceptance for interconnecting a single phase grid connected inverters (GCIs) with the utility grid owing to its straightforward implementation. This paper proposes a new design procedure to obtain the value of loop filter parameter of TD-PLL using time domain Performance Index Optimization based on non-linear optimization technique. The proposed tuning method was evaluated with established tuning methodologies under different grid disturbances. Numerical simulation results using MATLAB/ Simulink shows that the proposed tuning method provides an optimum parameter value and enable a better dynamic response without significant overshoot and steady state error in TD-PLL response.

articleTitle: Voltage and Frequency Control with Load Levelling of PMSG Based Small-Hydro System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, voltage and frequency control with load levelling of a small-hydro system using permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) is proposed. The power quality improvement of the system along with voltage and frequency controller (VFC) is realized using a voltage source converter (VSC) and a battery energy storage (BES) connected to its DC link. The VSC with BES, is also able to provide load compensation, load levelling and elimination of harmonics with voltage and frequency control. The battery maintains active power balance by charging during lightly loaded conditions. It also ensures supply of power, when the consumer load exceeds more than PMSG based hydro generation. A third order generalized integrator (TOGI) based control algorithm is used for generating the gating pulses to insulated gate bi-polar transistors (IGBTs) of VSC. This TOGI based control algorithm has a very simple structure and it behaves like a notch filter, which imposes less burden on the system. It only requires one parameter, a damping factor Ks for governing the control. This factor decides the stability, filtering capability and dynamic performance of the controller.

articleTitle: Locating The Source of Forced Oscillation in Power Systems using System Oscillating Energy
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The energy dissipation at the generator terminal is used to propose a technique to locate the source of forced oscillations in power systems. In the proposed technique, the network and the load dynamics are incorporated to accurately identify the source of the disturbance. It is also proved mathematically that the dissipating energy for the dominant natural mode of oscillation of a generator is related to damping parameter of that mode i.e. the real part of the eigenvalue of the linearized power system. The technique successfully locates all source of disturbance even when multiple sources of disturbance are applied at different times and durations. The impact of the damping of the electromechanical modes on the forced oscillations has been discussed and its effect on the proposed method of locating the disturbance is investigated. The method has been validated using simulations from various multimachine test systems containing single and multiple sources of forced oscillations.

articleTitle: Improved Internal Model Control based Closed Loop Controller Design for Second Order Piezoelectric System with Dead Time
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Precision control and positioning of devices at nanometer level have become ubiquitous in several industrial applications. Piezoelectric actuators offer flagship performance in this domain with its capability to actuate with resolution up to fraction of diameter of an atom. With important advantages like high accuracy, rapid response, high torque, compact form-factor they are being used several ultra-precise mechatronic systems. However, its performance is effected by severe nonlinearities, mostly hysteresis which needs to be tacked by proper controller design along with suitable plant model. This research first mathematically models the piezoelectric actuator as a second order plant using Dahl model for hysteresis. Parameters of the plant and nonlinear hysteretic term are experimentally identified using a commercially available piezoelectric actuator. An improved Internal Model Control approach is then explored which has a simpler structure than conventional IMC. As PID control is the most widely used control regime for practical usage, the research also presents an equivalent PID structure of the controller. The presence of system dead time has been considered and approximated using zero order `Pade' approximation. Results suggest an improvement in the controller response over a traditional control in terms of step response, impulse disturbance as well as noisy environment.

articleTitle: Discretization schemes Comparison for the Greenhouse Temperature Model
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A greenhouse is a covered structure that protects the plants from extensive external environment and creates a suitable growth environment using precise control strategy. In this paper, we suggest a suitable discretization method for the greenhouse temperature model by comparing conventionally used methods Runge-Kutta 4 (RK4) and Euler method with other discretization methods which includes explicit and embedded methods. These methods are compared on the basis of computational time and mean absolute error (MAE) as the performance criteria. Different methods have different computational time based on the complexity of its calculations, and their accuracy depends on the order of the method that is in consideration. On comparing the different methods, it is found that the Euler method is more suitable for the same sampling time of data with least computational burden, whereas with increasing sampling time Heun's method gives much better results.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Switching Techniques of DC-DC Converter for Improved Electric Vehicle Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The choice of an efficient dc-dc converter stage plays an important role in its designing, with proper selection of pulse width modulation (PWM) technique. In this paper ac-dc and dc-dc stages are implemented with PWM and asymmetrical pulse width modulation (APWM) technique respectively. The ac-dc stage vanishes the use of front end rectifier w hereas, in second stage there is no use of snubber circuit which helps dc-dc converter stage to decide zero voltage switching (ZVS) during turn-on process and zero current switching (ZCS) during turn-off process of electric vehicle (EV) battery charging. These switching is viable by using APWM and efficiency o f t he c onverter is also increase for 1.2 KW system in comparison with previously proposed PWM technique.

articleTitle: A Simple Fault Tolerant Multilevel Inverter Topology
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a fault tolerant seven level inverter topology. The operation of the inverter when one or more switches are faulted is presented in this paper. In case of any fault in the switches the power output is ensured though at reduced number of voltage levels, which increases the reliability of the system. The redundant switching states enables fault tolerant operation of the inverter. In case of faults in the bidirectional switches the power output along with the voltage levels is maintained. The proposed system is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Smart Household Energy Management by Employing EV and BESS as Enabling Technologies
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: As smart grid enabler, demand response programs have been a major attraction for reducing the peak demand in the electrical power system. The household user can contribute to significant potential for reduction in energy demand during peak hours. This paper is focused on the energy management of a single household equipped with several assets including home appliances, electric vehicle (EV) and battery energy storage system (BESS). A small-scale rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) generation is also a part of smart household. The BESS and PV are employed for charging home appliances, and if any surplus energy is available, it can fed back to grid. The optimization problem of smart household energy management is developed as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP). The electricity consumer is registered for real time prices based demand re- sponse programs by the load serving entity (LSE). The simulation results have exposed the significant contribution to gaining user cost benefits and peak to average ratio minimization for the LSE. By employing proposed approach the cost benefit of 87.06 Cents is achieved with 34.4 % peak to average ratio.

articleTitle: Distributed Control Strategy for the Coordinated Control Operation of the Distributed Generators
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a distributed control strategy for the coordinated control of multiple generators. A simple control strategy for primary as well as secondary control is proposed in this paper. The primary control consists of droop control which is analogous to the synchronous generator control. The primary control decides the power to be shared between the two distributed generators and regulates the voltage and frequency to the nominal values at point of common coupling, where the loads are present. The secondary control strategy allows the distributed generators to restore the frequency and voltage to the nominal values, if the primary control fails. The paper is free from the conventional d-q transformations. The developed controller possesses the features of adaptability and plug and play-in capability for smart grid interconnection. The performance of the proposed control strategy is validated through different numerical simulations and real-time implementations.

articleTitle: Voltage Drop Management and Step Up The Voltage of Sediment Microbial Fuel Cells
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Sediment microbial fuel cell (SMFC) is a bio-electrochemical device which produces the pollution-free energy. SMFC generates low voltage with fluctuation between 0.982 V to 1.16 V of 60 days of the experiment. This voltage is not suitable to power the electronic device. So an ultra-low voltage DC-DC boost converter is proposed to regulated and step up the output voltage of SMFC. Performance of the boost converter is verified through simulation and experimental results. Single SMFC discharges in 30 sec by connecting the boost converter and gain maximum voltage in 210 sec after disconnecting the boost converter. Further, a scheme proposed for continuous energy harvesting from sediment microbial fuel cell in which eight parallel connected SMFCs provide an input voltage to boost converter one by one. It is noticed that the energy harvester DC-DC boost converter provides a continuous 2.56 V with the efficiency of 85.46%. The boost converter works well up to the voltage of 20 mV so this converter is appropriate for the SMFC energy harvesting. The proposed scheme is able to produce a suitable voltage for a small electronic device which needs a continuous power supply.

articleTitle: Distributed Control Framework for Autonomous Seamless Operation of Electronically Interfaced Distributed Generators in AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for purely local information based, distributed control of low/medium voltage microgrids consisting of electronically interfaced despatchable energy resources. Apart from steady-state operation, emphasis is given to seamless transition of sources from grid connected mode to islanded mode and vice-versa. A synchronization approach for Island to Grid (I2G) transition and islanding detection for Grid to Island (G2I) transition is proposed by use of a novel concept of mode detection device, which considers all possible operating conditions of microgrid and thus demonstrate strong feasibility of its plug-and-play characteristics. Proposed methodology is supported with real time simulation results in RSCAD, run with Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) as well as a laboratory scale hardware setup.

articleTitle: Solar Power Based Single–Phase Transformerless Hybrid Series Active Filter based on Sliding Mode Controller for voltage and frequency deviations
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this work, a solar power based single phase Transformerless Hybrid Series Active power Filter (THSeAF) based on sliding mode controller (SMC) is proposed to mitigate voltage and frequency deviations in an Electrical Distribution System (EDS). To mitigate the voltage and frequency power quality issues, a THSeAF is used in this work. A solar power rating of 5.kW serves as an input to the THSeAF. An Auxiliary DC source is also provided to assist the solar power. A Boost converter is operated at a duty ratio of 0.4 to obtain desired output voltage of 400 V to be fed to the inverter circuit. A non- linear controller sliding mode control (SMC) is proposed to generate the firing pulses to the IGBT switches of the inverter in THSeAF. Stability of the system is derived using Bode plots by means of state feedback approach. The system is tested for voltage sag, swell, interruptions and frequency deviations. Simulations have been performed on PSCAD v4.6 with the controller operation on the load side of the system. It is observed through simulations that the THSeAF compensates for sag, swell and voltage harmonics with less THD (total harmonic distortion). A power factor improvement is also observed during the simulation work. The controller performance is found to be robust during the mitigation of the power quality issues. Desired compensation and THD within the limits are obtained which encourages for effective usage of this topology with SMC in distribution systems. This work can be extended using higher order SMC to reduce the chattering phenomenon.

articleTitle: Actuation Voltage Analysis Using FEM of RF MEMS Switch Design for Low Power Consumption Application
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper represents the analysis of RF MEMS perforated shunt switch which is designed on hafniumoxide substrate with stiff ribs around the membrane. The switch has used rectangular perforation with various sizes. With the help of perforation and adding serpentine meanders the problems of high actuation voltages, low switching speed, less flexibility and stiction in RF MEMS switch have been removed. The proposed switch attains high switching speed and low electrostatic actuation voltages. The perforation and meanders are joined with Fixed-fixed shunt switch. The pull in voltage provides maximum displacement in negative z-direction. The switch is designed on software COMSOL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> MULTIPHYSICS 4.3b.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of the Newfangled Cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In recent years multilevel inverters have been extensively worn in high voltage and high power applications for their unique performance. Reliability of the power electronic equipment is very essential to make sure that inverter operation should be stable and it is most important to detect and locate the faults as speedily as possible. This paper deals with open switch-fault finding method in a multilevel inverter using wavelet transformation tool. A fault diagnosis procedure is proposed and executed using MATLAB.

articleTitle: Real-time FuzzyLogic Based Power Quality Analysis of Hybrid microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper depicts voltage and current control of micro-grid system which is adequate to meet the power demand of local loads. The Hybrid microgrid considered in this work is a combination of a micro hydro based SEIG system, a PV array along with a Battery Energy Storage System(BESS) and a STATCOM. The SEIG system delivers a fixed amount of power to the loads. During load variation the SEIG does not have ample amount of power to serve the load requirement, so the system voltage and frequency fluctuations occurs and system performance deteriorates. To maintain the power quality the Fuzzy Controller based STATCOM is employed which supplies the required power to the loads. The active power demand of the load is managed by the dc side of the STATCOM which houses a PV-BESS system. The STATCOM controls the dc link voltage which on the other hand manages the active power flow to the load. The model has been simulated in real-time simulator for various load conditions like linear RL load, dynamic load and nonlinear load and the results are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: EGI Based Control for a Grid Tied Double Stage Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work proposes an enhanced generalized integrator (EGI) based control algorithm for a double stage grid connected solar photovoltaic (PV) system at adverse grid conditions like DC offset, variable solar insolation and voltage swell/sag. The main aim of this proposed EGI control algorithm is to extract the fundamental component from the grid voltage, even at adverse grid conditions. A perturb and observe (P&O) based MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) is used for peak power extraction from the PV array. Adaptive DC link voltage control is used for the reduction of VSC switching losses. The proposed system with EGI based control algorithm is simulated in MATLAB. The simulated performance is studied for various odd states like DC offset, voltage swell/sag, insolation change etc. For the validation of the test results, a prototype is built in the laboratory. THD (Total Harmonics Distortion) of the grid current during grid disturbances, is found in limits as recommended by the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Fractional Calculus Based PID Controller Tuned by SMO for LFC Application
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this investigation, to regulate the frequency a hybrid model having two area (thermal-hydro-wind & thermal-hydro-diesel) along with fractional order proportional integral derivative (FOPID) controller under MATLAB environment has been modelled. Further, the gain parameters of the offered controller are tuned with the help of recently introduced spider monkey optimization technique (SMO) by iterative method with ITAE (integral time absolute error) as the cost/objective function. At first, the modelled system is verified with the presence of AC tie-line. Further sensitivity comparative analysis has been done by amplifying the loading of the system by 15% with SMO tuned classical PID controller and offered FOPID controller. Finally, investigation of vigorous responses reveals that SMO tuned FOPID controller yield minimum oscillations on the basis of overshoot and undershoot as well as least settling time as compared to PID controller under above-mentioned circumstances.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Real-time Performance Analysis of Buck-regulator Fed Current Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced buck-regulator fed current source inverter and the performance analysis of the same is compared with conventional voltage source inverter (VSI) and current source inverter (CSI). In many applications such as brushless dc motors and stepper motors, a square or modified square wave ripple free current for certain period of time is required. However, with pulse width modulation (PWM) voltages and currents obtained at the output of conventional VSI and CSI contains harmonics. A buck-regulator fed CSI is capable of minimizing the voltage and current ripples even if PWM technique is employed. Hence, the harmonic distortion analysis for both load current and voltage delivered by VSI, CSI and buck-regulator fed CSI are performed in this paper. The analyses are performed with traditional 120° conduction and with multiple carriers based PWM approach. Presently buck-regulator fed CSI has been widely implemented in special motor drives applications. The compared converters are validated with a fixed RL load both in simulation as well as a prototype developed in the laboratory. Results shows that with the use of an inductor with reduced number of turns, the ripples in the output current for the buck-regulator fed CSI is minimized significantly compared to a conventional CSI and hence load side filter can be avoided.

articleTitle: Xilinx FPGA Based Single Phase Five-Level Cascaded Z-Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a single phase five-level cascaded Z-source inverter with reduced number of switches for PV/FC/Wind power applications. The inherent benefits of z-source inverter are higher boost gain and fault ride through capability compared with the traditional VSI and CSI inverters. Therefore five-level Z-source converter is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment and the generation of control pulses with the help of Xilinx System Generator is presented. A prototype model is developed to validate the theoretical concepts through experimental and simulation results.

articleTitle: Modified Gating Signal Controlled High-Frequency Transformer Isolated LCL-T Type DC-DC Resonant Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a LCL-T type of resonant power converter using modified gating signals is proposed for PV applications. The fixed-frequency modified gating is adopted to process and control the power flow in the circuit. The converter is designed to operate in lagging pf mode to ensure zero-voltage switching (ZVS) of the inverter switches. Fourier series method is used to analyze the converter in steady-state. The main advantage of LCL-T converter is that it provides protection against load short circuit. It is shown that a small change in pulse width is required to regulate the output voltage for variations in input voltage and load. A 300 W converter is designed and its performance is studied using PSIM simulations. Power loss breakdown analysis is performed.

articleTitle: A Transformerless Doubly Boost DC-DC Converter for grid connetced solar photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A transformer-less doubly boost DC-DC converter (DBDC) is proposed in this paper. This converter can provide higher gain as compared to conventional boost converter and has reduced component count as compared to existing non-isolated high-gain dc-dc converters. Owing to its high gain capability it can be employed in schemes having low voltage input viz. solar PV, fuel cell, battery etc. The derivation of the converter and its possible application in grid connected solar PV systems is discussed in details. The salient features of the overall scheme includes: high efficiency, low value of DC bus capacitances, low leakage current, low cost, less size and light weight. To ascertain effectiveness of this scheme detailed simulation studies are carried out in Matlab/Simulink. The operation of the scheme is examined under different irradiance levels and the capability to track maximum power point is ascertained through incremental conductance algorithm. The operating principle of DBDC, control structure of overall scheme, and the results obtained from the exhaustive simulation studies are presented in detail.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Capability with Seamless Transition of Three-Phase Grid using FLMF Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a grid connected mode (GCM) and standalone mode (SAM) of the photovoltaic (PV) - battery based microgrid system. Whenever the grid fails, this system transfers from GCM to SAM without causing any interruption to the load supply. In the similar context, after the restoration of the grid, the system goes into GCM of operation. In the GCM, the voltage source converter (VSC) of microgrid, operates in current control mode (CCM) and in SAM, it operates in voltage control mode (VCM). A bidirectional DC-DC converter (BDDC), controls the charging and discharging of the battery in GCM and in SAM. In SAM, the BDDC performs the extraction of PV array maximum power by regulating the DC link voltage to the PV array maximum power point (MPP) voltage. In GCM, the VSC performs the extraction of PV array maximum power. The BDDC is used for interconnecting the solar PV array and the battery; hence the second order harmonic is not fed to the battery so the effective life of the battery is increased. The VSC performs the seamless transition from SAM to GCM and vice versa and it also performs multi-functions such as harmonics mitigation, balancing of grid currents and unity power factor (UPF) operation in GCM.

articleTitle: A Comparative study of a T-type Asymmetrical Multilevel Inverter with Two Different Sources with Conventional H-bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a comparative study of a T-type Asymmetrical multilevel inverter (ASMLI) with two sources namely a Battery as a low voltage source and solar with boost converter as a higher voltage source is analyzed with respect to a conventional H Bridge Converter. Two switches with an antiparallel diode are used to modulate the low voltage level and a conventional VSI is used to obtain a high voltage level in the power circuit. A state space model is derived and stability analysis is performed. A vertical shifted SPWM control is used for obtaining switching mechanism of the ASMLI circuit. The analytical study ASMLI is interfaced between the low level input voltage sources solar and/or battery with the AC load or AC grid. It is observed that the system is well stable by taking the output voltage and inductor current. A comparison with a conventional H-Bridge inverter is brought about through various cases with single source. Total Harmonic Distortion, conduction losses, efficiency, voltage and current stresses are in detail compared and derived that this inverter is capable for applications for power ratings less than 100 KW. Also the stress and rate of change of current on the front end Boost converter is found to be approximately 50% less compared to a conventional based DC-AC configuration. The simulation is performed in PSCAD v4.6 and observation is done for 5 kW load with different power factor's and also with different modulation indexes. For medium and low power applications, T-type Asymmetrical multilevel inverter (ASMLI) can be preferred.

articleTitle: Effective Switching Sequence Scheme for Space Vector Modulated Two-Level Inverter to Reduce the Current Distortion in Linear Operating Range
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the scheme for effective selection of switching sequences to improve the performance of two-level three-phase space vector modulated voltage source inverter. In conventional space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) for two-level inverters, amongst the eight voltage vectors desired voltage reference vector is generated by applying the switching sequence 0-1-2-7 in a given sampling time period in a first sector of the hexagon shaped space vector diagram. The placement of these voltage vectors with their dwell times gives the inverter output under its linear operating range. The generated inverter voltage with its non-sinusoidal nature imposes the application restrictions. It is proposed to utilize the switching vectors available with different combination of their switching sequences to reduce the stator flux ripple, generated voltage and current distortions. Five such switching sequences 0-1-2-7 (conventional), 0-1-2-1, 1-0-1-2, 2-7-2-1, 7-2-1-2 are taken into consideration and presented with their effective improvements in the inverter output voltages and in turn reflected into the load current distortion. Inverter performance is presented under the linear range of its operation and suggested the variable speed drive application. The results are validated with laboratory hardware prototype.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Double-sided Slot Antenna Using Close-coupled Biasing Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable slot antenna that uses a close-coupled biasing technique to facilitate the reconfiguring between two frequency bands. The technique uses a very thin double layered flexible copper clad Mylar substrate with the slot antenna on the front side and the biasing circuits at the backside of the design. The biasing circuit uses a conventional PIN diode to switch between ON and OFF states. Each state corresponds to a separate operating band. The reconfiguring from one sub-band to another is done electronically by means of a BAR64 diode. In this first example, the two bands are located close to each other to increase the bandwidth of the antenna. The resulting -10dB bandwidth increases by 20% as compared with the OFF-state. The antenna has mostly omnidirectional radiation patterns at the two frequency bands. Simulation and measurement results are compared and discussed which are to be in good agreement with one another.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Torque Ripple in BLDC Motor using Modified SEPIC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Commutation torque ripple in brushless DC motor (BLDCM) is a major key issue, which mainly introduces during the speed change and outgoing as well as incoming phase current changing at a different rate on the same time. Hence, this paper presents a novel technique to suppress commutation torque ripple of BLDCM using a DC-DC converter circuit. A comprehensive analysis of torque ripple is carried out in commutation as well as conduction region. A modified single-ended primary inductor converter (MSEPIC) has been employed in front of the three-phase inverter to mitigate the commutation torque ripple. The switch selector circuit and its control technique have been introduced to obtained desire input dc voltage at the commutation interval. The proposed novel technique is designed in MATLAB/Simulink software. The dynamic behavior of the proposed circuit has been studied. Simulation results of the proposed system and conventional BLDCM drive are presented to validate the system effectiveness.

articleTitle: Impact of Optimal Scheduling of DRs and Network Reconfiguration on the Performance of Active Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Contemporary distribution systems can be seen with remote operated line switches and optimally placed distributed generations (DGs) and shunt capacitors (SCs). Though these components can effectively reduce power losses and also improve node voltage profiles, however, in actual practice their impact is different under varying system states. A detailed investigation is presented in the paper to show the impact of distributed resources (DRs) power control and network reconfiguration (NR) for different system states of distribution systems. More realistic problem formulation is presented by considering load diversity among distribution buses. Recently developed variant of cat swarm optimization is employed as an optimization tool. Detailed investigations carried on a standard test bench shows the relevance of present study for distribution network operators.

articleTitle: Newfangled Multilevel Inverter fed V/f Controlled Induction Motor Drive with Multicarrier PWM Strategy
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In the modern industrial drive system, power electronic converters are employed not only to control the electromechanical energy conversion process, but also facilitate energy efficiency and continued automation. In the drive system, induction motor (IM) is a preferred energy conversion device because of its inherent features. Nowadays, power converters using MLI's playing vital role in the energy conversion process also multilevel configuration allow raising the power-handling capability of the system. Thus, in this paper fifteen level cascaded MLI fed closed loop V/f controlled IM drive is developed and its performance indicators have been analyzed for multicarrier carrier PWM strategy executed using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Design and development of electro mechanical bistable functions using shape memory alloy
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: An attempt has been made to realize electro mechanical bistable logic functions using shape memory alloy (SMA) which can exhibit functionalities similar to that of electronic logic devices. Titanium-nickel (TiNi) based SMAs are widely used because of its large work output per unit of actuator mass thereby enabling miniaturization; moreover, it can be used in harsh working environments. The paper presents implementation of bistable logic states in terms of NOT, OR, and NOR logics and its combinatorial application, the digital to analog converter (DAC) using suitable configurations / structures with SMA wire actuators. The basic and common structural configuration comprises of a nitinol wire, a bias spring, a slotted disc and a shaft. The SMA wire is wound as a loop through the peripheral slots of the disc and its ends are connected to a supporting member. The rod passes via the central slot of the disc and is engaged with the bias spring around it, which helps in restraining the SMA wire during the cooling cycle. The actuation of SMA moves the rod; the displacement of the rod is marked as the output. These designs are not based on linkage mechanisms; are implemented in MESO scales and could later be translated into the micro domain.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Quasi Z-Source Based T-Type Seven-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new structure of Hybrid Quasi Z-source based T-type seven-level inverter for renewable applications. The proposed topology comprises of three quasi Z-source based impedance networks cascaded with a T-type seven-level inverter structure consisting of H-bridge and bidirectional switches. The bidirectional switches operate at high frequency and are utilized for level generation. Only two switches in the H-bridge are utilized for shoot-through insertion, while the other two switches operate at the fundamental frequency. The proposed switching scheme along with the different operating modes are addressed for each level generation and the simulation is carried out in Matlab software to verify the performance. An experimental setup is also developed to validate the simulation results. Further, the merits of the proposed topology are highlighted with the comparison of recently proposed topologies.

articleTitle: State Estimation for Cascaded Hybrid Multi-level Inverter Fed Induction Motor Drive Using Derivative-free Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Induction machines are extensively used electrical machines in industrial applications. Now-a-days, energy efficient high power rated electrical drives are attracted by industries. Multi-level inverter fed induction motor drives provide a good solution for energy efficient drives. In multilevel inverters due complexity of switching patterns, there is more chance of fault occurring situations. For incipient fault detection, model based methods are gaining importance now-a days. In this paper, state estimation for cascaded hybrid Multilevel inverter fed induction motor using derivative-free extended Kalman filter is presented. With ready available current sensors, the proposed method is very effective for estimating dynamic behaviour of the induction motor drive. Additionally, the technique is very effective for accurate fault detection. Extensive simulation studies are performed on 3.7 kW induction motor using Matlab/Simulink 2016a environment. The presented results validates that proposed methodology can be used in realistic applications.

articleTitle: Space Vector PWM Techniques for Parallel Connected Dual-Split-Phase IMs for Full Power Range Using Capacitive Filters
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper describes a novel space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) scheme for the decoupled control of two parallel connected split phase induction machines operated from a single six-phase VSI which acts as a power source. To limit the flow of non-torque producing current, two switched capacitor filters are added. It is possible to operate both the motors at full rated power with low switching frequency, and decoupled control for full power range can be achieved. This is possible because the individual machines in the proposed configuration do not carry the load and harmonic currents of other machine (as in the case of conventional series/parallel connected machines). Two different schemes of SVPWM techniques are discussed and compared. Experimental results for both the schemes are provided in this paper.

articleTitle: Modified Space Vector Modulated Three-phase to Three-phase Matrix Converter Under Unbalanced Supply Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a study of modified space vector modulation technique (MSVM) for matrix converter (MC) which produces balanced output voltages in presence of unbalanced supply voltage conditions. The conventional modulation techniques derived for balanced supply conditions give poor performance in presence of abnormal input voltage conditions. Modified modulation techniques use actual input voltages for calculation of instantaneous modulation index which compensates disturbances present on input side and produces balanced output voltages. MSVM incorporates the actual input voltage characteristics for calculating modulation index and input modulation angle which produce required output voltages in presence of unbalanced supply conditions. The effectiveness of MSVM technique is verified and compared with conventional SVM technique by simulation performed in PSIM environment.

articleTitle: Self-sensing characteristics and analysis of the stiffness of the SMA spring actuator
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research work is aimed to study the relationship between electrical resistance and stiffness of shape memory alloy (SMA) spring actuator. Self-sensing refers to the measurement of resistance of SMA along with the actuation of actuator. It is used to calculate its stiffness directly, instead of using a stiffness sensor. Despite investing numerous efforts in creating a reliable, robust self-sensing actuator, not much success has been achieved till now. This paper proposes a self-sensing for SMA spring actuator for stiffness measurement and its analysis. Voltage across SMA spring and known series resistance is used to establish the stiffness. Experiments are conducted to investigate the relationship between electrical resistance and stiffness of SMA spring actuator. To evaluate the characteristics between stiffness and resistance an experimental set up comprising of a steel spring biased SMA spring actuator is used. The SMA spring actuator is heated electrically with varying activation current and frequencies and then the corresponding stiffness is calculated from force and displacement. The polyfit model facilitates to replace the additional sensor and electronics for stiffness sensor. A qualitative agreement between simulated and experimental stiffness is observed. It provide scope for sensor less control by simplifying the control system. To make SMA more applicable to small scale robotic manipulations, its stiffness control using accurate self - sensing is best alternative.

articleTitle: Generalized Normalized Gradient Descent Based Control Algorithm for Solar PV Integrated 3P4W Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a generalized normalized gradient descent (GNGD) based intelligent control algorithm for a solar PV array integrated 3-phase 4-wire distribution system. This system is based on single stage topology. It contains a three-phase 4-leg two level voltage source inverter (VSC), which executes multi-task functions, depending upon the system requirement and operating condition. It extracts the peak power from the solar PV array, improves the grid current power quality by mitigating the load current harmonics, reduces the reactive power burden and provides the load balancing on the distribution system and mitigates the AC mains neutral current. The VSC is controlled by GNGD based intelligent control algorithm, which estimates the magnitude of the fundamental component of load current. Instead of using a priori error concept to update the weight, this control algorithm uses a posteriori error based concept to improve the steady state performance. The incremental and conductance (INC) based control algorithm is utilized to extract the peak power from the PV array. The performance of the control algorithm is validated through simulation results and test results obtained on a developed laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Real Time Energy Management System and Control Strategy for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work is dedicated towards the design, configuration and ratings of various structural components of DC microgrid. Optimal voltage levels for DC distribution systems are also discussed based on efficiency studies of various converters. Real time energy management system (RTEMS) and controlling schemes are investigated for a grid tied DC microgrid comprising of various configuration blocks. The presented work deals with the dynamic controlling of intermittent power sources such as photovoltaic unit which increases the complexity of the integrated control algorithm. The proposed microgrid configuration and RTEMS is successfully implemented in RSCAD software. System dynamics originating due to variation in loading conditions, temperature and solar insolation are also observed and detailed in this work. Implementation of RTEMS ensures stable DC node voltages under such heavy transients. The power equilibrium is discussed for various system conditions.

articleTitle: Prototype Non-Volatile FPGA SVPWM Controller for 3-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a prototype non-volatile FPGA space vector pulse width modulated digital controller for 3-level inverter. Algorithm for digital controller is first realized using simulink blocks from HDL coder library of matlab. HDL coder transforms simulink model to fine and synthesizable very high speed integrated circuit hardware description language. Synthesis and execution tools generate bit stream of the code and it is executed to flash memory of FPGA. The developed prototype FPGA digital controller is validated on a 3-level inverter that energize three-phase open-end winding induction motor. Excellent harmonic performance is observed in real time spectral analysis of phase voltage and current of the motor. This development technique enables engineers to construct, simulate, authenticate and develop advanced schemes within small duration of time.

articleTitle: Single Stage SEGS Tied to the Three Phase Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-objective novel ESASMA (Exponential Sparsity-Aware Set-Membership Adaptive) based control strategy for grid tied single stage SEGS (Solar Energy Generating System). The ESASMA method is utilized for fundamental load component harvesting, when load current is non-linear. Moreover, ESASMA approach is also used for power quality improvement at PCC in both conditions either with solar power generation or absence. In this way, power converters is used at its extreme level, consequently, payback time is reduced, and proposed system becomes economical. For validation of proposed approach, a system is examined in various test condition on developed hardware prototype.

articleTitle: Reduced Flux based Direct Torque Control of Synchronous Reluctance Machine for Electric Vehicle applications
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Synchronous reluctance motors (SyRMs) generate electromagnetic torque that depend on the saliency of the rotor structure. SyRMs are seen as attractive alternative to permanent magnet machines in applications that require high dynamic performance, high power density etc. A new direct torque control (DTC) scheme is proposed in this paper for the SyRM aimed at improving overall performance of the motor especially under light load conditions. This is accomplished by dynamically adjusting the motor stator flux based on the load conditions. Analytical expressions for the required stator flux is presented in detail. Furthermore, the proposed idea is extended to an electric vehicle (EV) application and benefits of the envisaged DTC scheme is thoroughly investigated considering constant speed-constant load torque, constant speed-variable load torque conditions and is also tested using Inspection and Maintenance drive cycle (IM240) for testing the variable speed-constant load torque condition. Superior performance of the proposed reduced flux based DTC scheme for SyRM over the conventional DTC scheme is presented. The SyRM draws less current for a given torque, results in reduced ripple content in the electromagnetic torque developed and more importantly achieves improved motor efficiency thus facilitating improved energy savings which is a useful feature desired in EV applications.

articleTitle: Control of Renewable Energy Integrated Universal Active Filter for Modern Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work proposes a novel control technique for the control of universal active power filter with distribution generation capabilities (UAPF-DG). The proposed technique uses a complex filter to estimate the per phase active component of load current in a three phase system. The methodology uses complex filter to obtain fundamental balanced positive sequence component of distorted load current. This is used in reference generation of shunt active filter of UAPF-DG. This technique is inherently a three phase technique and involves lower computational burden The UAPF-DG system regulates the voltage of sensitive loads while simultaneously compensating the nonlinear load currents, thus achieving unity power at point of common coupling (PCC). The performance of the proposed system is validated on an experimental setup and tested for its response under conditions of load unbalance, voltage rise/dip and variation in solar irradiation.

articleTitle: Wavelet Ridge Based Technique to Detect the Presence of Sustained Oscillation in Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a technique to detect the presence of sustained oscillation is detected. The proposed method utilizes the wavelet ridge technique to extract the oscillating trend underlying the noisy signal. Autocorrelation of the extracted signal is used to find the periodicity present in the signal and then the frequency present in the oscillation is estimated using power spectral density. Sustained nature of the oscillation is decided by calculating the probability density function of the damping present in the signal. The proposed method is a threshold-free technique and hence very effective in the detection of the sustained oscillation. The proposed method is verified using measurements from the simulated test system, New England test system, field phasor measurement data and IEEE benchmark forced oscillation cases.

articleTitle: Cooperative Energy Scheduling of Microgrids with Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an energy management framework for a distribution system comprising of multiple cooperative microgrids. The energy management framework aims at reducing the energy cost of the microgrids by minimizing the grid purchases which comprises of conventional generation. The intermittencies associated with renewable energy based-energy sources are modelled in the proposed framework through scenarios. Within this stochastic framework, a power exchange model is embedded that allows local power exchanges between neighboring microgrids, with the objective of optimally alleviating the distribution power losses. Extensive numerical results are shown to corroborate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Real Time Implementation of Solar PV Energy System under Weak Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-magnitude integrator quadrature signal generator (MMI-QSG) based adaptive control to take care the grid abnormalities during the operation of voltage source converter (VSC) of a grid tied PV generating system (GTPGS). In proposed topology, the VSC performs as a PV array power DC-AC conversion supplying active power with the active power filter (APF) capabilities thus taking care the power quality (PQ) issues simultaneously; and a boost convertor is utilized here for implementation of P&O (Perturb and observe) based method for maximum power tracking (MPT) and MMI-QSG for the extraction of FC (Fundamental Component) of grid voltage and load current. The GTPGS is flexible as it continues to work satisfactorily under weak grid conditions and presence of nonlinear load connected at the PCC (Point of Common Coupling). The MMI consists of magnitude integrator, which has characteristic of accurate integration and retains a behavior of perfect FOS (First Order System) in terms of magnitude. The second order generalized integrator (SOGI) has simple and flexible structure, however, its dynamic response is affected by the damping gain and input and output parameters of the system. Accordingly, the design of the structure is complex. The MMI-QSG is configured to determine the fundamental component (FC) of current and voltage. The proposed MMI-QSG based control supports the PV array interfaced VSC to satisfy the grid voltage control requirements under several grid voltage distortion conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed structure of MMI-QSG method is evaluated through test results on the developed prototype in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Single Phase Solar Inverter with Inertia Emulation
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Synchronous machines or alternators form the core of the power generation capability in the traditional electrical power system. They have a rotating flywheel which enables them to impart stability to the grid. With the increasing penetration of distributed renewable energy sources, DC to AC conversion systems has gained huge popularity. Proper stable operation of the electrical grid depends on the fact that the alternator has a rotating flywheel(mechanical inertia), which can quickly absorb or release energy in a controlled manner. The flywheel is not available for a traditional DC to AC converter i.e. inverter used in renewable energy conversions. This is where the idea of an inverter with emulated inertia can play a significant role. It can convert energy efficiently from DC sources to AC for further transmission of power through the grid and still retain all the features of a traditional alternator that help in stabilising the grid. In this paper, focus has been put on single phase inverters as single phase inverters on home rooftops form a huge segment of the future renewable energy generation prospect. Moreover, renewable energy sources always have an element of unpredictability associated with it. Injection of this unpredictable amount of power into the grid makes the grid more unstable. So, with steady increase in the use of inverters powered by renewable energy sources, such inertia emulation ability is essential for grid-connected inverters to keep the stability of the grid intact, especially in rapidly changing atmospheric conditions where the amount of available renewable energy keeps varying. To solve this problem, the idea of single phase solar inverter with inertia emulation is proposed here. Calculations have been shown here to estimate the capacity of energy storage required for proper operation. The proposed inverter is controlled through synchronous reference frame based control method instead of popularly used hysteresis based methods, which allows for superior quality power to be injected to the grid.

articleTitle: PV Connected Grid-tied Discreet Current Controller for Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the three phase four wire (TPFW) single-stage PV array connected grid tied distribution system using discreet multiple complex coefficient filter (DMCCF) technique for compensating the harmonics of load currents and to eliminate the switching ripple of PCC (Point of Common Coupling) voltage. Due to use of various nonlinear loads in distribution system, harmonics are injected and effect the overall system. The maximum PV power is extracted using maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm. To eliminate the harmonics and to balance the grid currents, DMCCF control is used, which injects the required reactive component, and maintains the grid currents according to the IEEE 519 standard. Moreover, the active power is injected in to the grid, which eliminates the harmonics in the grid currents. Using this controller, the fundamental reference grid currents are estimated. To reduce the dependency on PI (Proportional Integral) controller and for improved the dynamic response, a PV array power feed-forward term is used. This control improves the dynamic response when insolation is changed. Moreover, the power quality issues are incorporated like balancing, power factor correction and reduced the grid side currents harmonics. Test results has shown the compensation of nonlinear loads and improved steady-state and dynamic performances of the system and neutral current compensation.

articleTitle: Risk-constrained Energy Management of Cooperative Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The problem of coordinated energy management of multiple-coupled microgrids is considered in the proposed work. The framework aims at regulating the inter-microgrid and grid power exchanges, with the objective of minimizing the distribution power losses. Within this framework, a risk control scheme is embodied, that regulates the volatility associated with the expected profits of microgrids due to various system uncertainties. Results corroborate the efficacy of the proposed framework in reducing power losses and renewable energy curtailments, while maintaining a tradeoff between maximizing the microgrid profits and controlling its variability.

articleTitle: MAF-SOGI-PLL based Single-Phase Multimode PV-Battery System with Improved Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a single phase multimode photovoltaic (PV)-battery system which can provide harmonics compensation and reactive power support along with extracting maximum power from PV array in current control mode and an uninterrupted power supply mode to loads during the grid outage. The PV-battery system consists of a buck-boost converter for the battery and a voltage sourced converter (VSC). The buck-boost converter facilitates battery charging and maintains DC link voltage at reference value. The VSC has a multimode controller, which uses a SOGI based Laplacian Kernel current controller for grid connected mode, a dq-frame based voltage controller for standalone mode, an islanding detection and mode transition mechanism. A hybrid islanding detection method using ROCOFOP (Rate of Change of Frequency over Power) and a MAF-SOGI-PLL based voltage monitoring mechanism, monitors the grid condition. Based on its output, the multimode controller decides the mode of operation and static transfer switch (STS) position and synchronization is carried out as per the IEEE 1547-2018 revised standard. Experimental results show the performance of the controller in catering to the the set objectives.

articleTitle: Primary Frequency Response Constrained Interruptible Load Scheduling Under PV Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Protean demand pattern with the rise in environmental concerns are the driving factors towards integration of renewable energy source (RES). Incorporation of RES generation, lead to displacement of conventional generators and hence causes a decline in the system inertia and Primary Frequency Response (PFR) capability. Moreover, RES uncertain characteristics would further dwindle in systems inherent inertia and PFR capability. This arises concern for the system operator to maintain reliability and security of the system particularly at the time of contingency like largest generator outage or loss of a large block of the load. This imbalances between generation and load require an additional response for maintaining system stability. In this regard, present work signifies the need of an additional response from the Interruptible load (IL) in presence of uncertain PV penetration. The uncertainty of the PV is being handled by the ARIMA model. Present work introduces a potential role of IL in day ahead stochastic unit commitment (SUC) framework considering PV uncertainty. Case studies are implemented on one area IEEE RTS 24 bus system considering 30% penetration level of PV. Simulation results would assess the validation of role played by IL in enhancing system frequency parameters under uncertain PV power.

articleTitle: Design of Modular Multilevel Converter for micro grid inked photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a technique which employs two stage power conversion of output obtained from photovoltaic systems. In the present situation power generation from conventional sources needs to be reduced and it is more focused on non conventional sources. In this paper power generation from solar energy is emphasized. The array of photo-voltaic (PV) panels is connected to establish the dc link. DC link obtained from the PV array is input to DC-DC converter and the voltage obtained from converter is administered as input to modular multilevel converter. Depending upon the requirement the output is fed to the micro-grid or to the load. In order to increase the efficiency of entire PV generation system maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is employed. In addition to MPPT, control scheme has been introduced to escalate the performance of MMC. This paper presents an outcome of implementing Perturb & Observe (P&O) method along with hysteresis current controller for MMC. The performance of proposed system in PV environment is verified by simulation results and results are validated.

articleTitle: A Novel Reduced Device Count Multilevel Inverter Structure using Non-isolated Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present a novel structure of multilevel inverter (MLI). The proposed structure uses 4 number of equal non-isolated DC sources, 8 number of unidirectional switches and 1 bidirectional switch. The structure is able to generate 9 output voltage levels across the load terminals. A detailed comparison study with recently published MLI structures shows that the proposed structure is able to produce output voltage levels using minimum number of switches, drivers and provides minimum TSV (Total Standing Voltage) with respect to other structures. Further, the comparison of overall cost of different structures is presented by considering a CF (Cost Function). It has been observed that the proposed structure provides lowest cost function as compared to other topologies at same output voltage level. The proposed structure is analyzed for low frequency as well as for high frequency modulation strategies. The performance of the structure is verified by an extensive simulation study in MATLAB/Simulink for low as well as high frequency modulation strategies under different load conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Conventional and Electric powertrain
publicationTitle: 2018 8th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: To curb rising environmental pollution, energy issues and depletion of petroleum sources, electric vehicle (EV) is a cleaner, reliable and efficient transport system. Out of all electric motors employed in electric powertrain, permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is the most economical one because of its high power and torque density. This paper presents the evaluative study of driving performance of powertrain propelled by two different systems. The characteristics of conventional generic engine are analyzed to extract the essential requirements that are necessary to implement the required model of the electric powertrain using the appropriate properties of electric motor. The electric motor is controlled via three phase voltage source inverter (VSI) in which the space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) technique is employed for switching control of VSI.
